title: Reading: new tome and scroll odds

sections.heading: Scholar
items: Every book you read through has a fixed chance to hold a spell tome or a scroll, by rank. Tomes: Novice 1 in 143, Apprentice 1 in 167, Adept 1 in 333, Expert 1 in 625, Master 1 in 2,500. Scrolls: Novice 1 in 57, Apprentice 1 in 67, Adept 1 in 80, Expert 1 in 250, Master 1 in 600.
Each rank opens at a Scholar level: Novice for everyone, Apprentice at 25, Adept at 50, Expert at 75 and Master at 90. Higher Scholars still find the lower ranks.
A reading gives at most one tome or scroll. There is no daily limit, and finding one does not lower your chances afterwards.
Expert and Master spell tomes still come only to the Senior ranks of a college.

sections.heading: Smithing
items: Any Orc can now forge Orcish armour and weapons, whether or not they belong to a stronghold. Only Orcs can make them. The Orcish Clan pieces stay with the strongholds' own smiths.

sections.heading: Courts
items: You can now leave a court you serve on your own: type /court resign followed by the hold's name (for example /court resign Bruma). You give up your post and leave its household, and a citizenship that came with the post ends with it. A ruler steps down through the staff.
A Step down button in your journal's Court tab (F3) follows with the next client update.

sections.heading: Writing spell tomes
items: Master Scholars write spell tomes at a Scholars' Ledger: choose Write a spell tome. You can write a tome of a spell you know, as long as a tome of it exists.
Novice tomes need no scrolls. Apprentice tomes need 1 scroll, Adept 2 and Expert 4. These can be any scrolls you carry, and the cheapest go first.

A Master tome needs 5 scrolls of that same spell, and a co-writer: a Master of the spell's school (a Master Priest for Restoration) who knows the spell, stands within 10 metres of you and agrees. You do not need to know a Master spell yourself.

After you write a tome, you wait before you can write another, whatever its rank: a day after a Novice tome, 2 days after Apprentice, 4 after Adept, a week after Expert and two weeks after Master. A co-writer waits the two weeks too.
Tomes of raising the dead and of calling or banishing Daedra are still written only by senior college ranks.

sections.heading: Writing scrolls
items: Master Scholars also write scrolls of the spells they know, at the same ledger: choose Write a scroll. Master scrolls cannot be written.
Each scroll uses 1 Linen Wrap, 1 Charcoal (from woodcutting) and 1 filled soul gem of any size. The smallest gem is used first.
Scrolls have their own wait, apart from tomes: a day after a Novice scroll, 2 days after Apprentice, 3 after Adept and 4 after Expert.
Both waits are shown on the Scholar page of the Skills tab in your journal (F3), and at the top of both lists.

sections.heading: Colleges
items: Any magic college now counts the same as the Synod, the College of Winterhold and the College of Whispers: its leader and officers can teach classes at a Class Lectern and take on more apprentices.

title: Client 0.3.103: field of view, referrals and the bank

sections.heading: Client 0.3.103
items: Field of view now sticks: the value you set in the launcher is put on the game camera when you spawn, after the character creator and after a load, instead of sometimes being lost.
New field of view slider in F3, Settings, Camera. Move it between 50 and 140 and the view changes as you drag. Your choice is kept for your next start, and Reset puts the launcher's value back.

New Referrals tab in the F3 journal: your invite link and code, how far each friend you invited has got, and your rewards. A new account can enter a friend's code there once, in its first 24 hours of play.

Item vaults are open: rent a Strongbox (100 weight), a Coffer (250 weight) or a Vault (500 weight) at one gold per weight a week at a hold's bank, from the bank panel. Each hold's bank keeps its own vault, and an unpaid vault is seized after 30 days.
Gold piles and coin purses lying around the world can no longer be taken: they give nothing now. Gold comes from work, trade and taxes. Gold another player drops can still be picked up.
The Pale Pass border gates between Skyrim and Cyrodiil stand closed again instead of looking wide open. Walk up to the gate and use it to cross.

sections.heading: Elections
items: A hold's first election does not ask for seven days of citizenship, and that includes whether it starts: the 15 citizens a hold needs to begin its first election are counted without the seven days. No character has yet been a citizen of a hold for a week, so the rule was leaving every hold with nought voters - and because a hold's citizen count is the number who may vote, it read as nought citizens too. Nobody was removed from any roll.

Everything else still holds for a first vote: the Discord account's age and the hours and days of play are judged as always, and the hold's Voting tab still tells you which one you are missing and when you will meet it.
Once a hold has seated a court by election, every later election there asks for the seven days, including one that staff restart.

The Rift's election, which opened before these rules existed, keeps its courts and its closing time: the rules were applied to it where it stands, as its first election, rather than starting it again. From the vote's opening a Rift voter needs the Discord account's age and the hours and days of play above; the seven days are not asked. Nobody has to re-enter a court.

title: Falkreath, Dawnguard crossbows and Summon Skeleton

sections.heading: The world
items: Falkreath is fully back to its Cities of the North layout: the floating slabs and rocks, the hole by the wall and the white streak are gone.

sections.heading: Smithing
items: Dawnguard smiths can forge the Dawnguard crossbows and bolts again, the enhanced and exploding ones included.

sections.heading: Magic
items: Summon Skeleton works for every caster again: everyone gets the regular skeleton until the beast-race skeletons are added.
The admin panel's Give all spells and Give all shouts are gone for good.

sections.heading: Treasuries
items: The Pale now has a treasury at the Dawnstar bank. It starts with 10,000 gold, the same starting treasury every other hold received.
Taxes and fees paid in The Pale now go into that treasury, so the Jarl of the Pale has tax income like the other holds.

sections.heading: Spells
items: Incite Hysteria, Split the Mind, Blinding Mist, Shroud of Endurance and Shroud of Fortitude are held back for now: their effect on other people and creatures only happened on the caster's own screen. They stay in your spellbook.
The unlocking spells (Unlock Container and Open) are held back for now: locks are kept by the server, and these spells only work on the caster's own screen.
Two more joke summons have left the realm's magic: Sir Roderic the slaughterfish and the jar bomb.

sections.heading: Draugr
items: Draugr are no longer far tougher than other foes of their rank, and their blows and shouts land a quarter softer. Deathlords are still the hardest fight of their level.

sections.heading: Spells
items: Summoned mounts (Summon Indrik, Ethereal Strider, Arvak) are held back for now: riding a summoned mount wasn't shown to other players and could crash the game. They stay in your spellbook.
Conjure Ent is held back for now: it could crash the game when it appeared.
Spells that only worked on the caster's own screen are held back until they work for everyone: the Arnima turrets, Earthen Barrier, Earthen Pillar, Protective Vortex, Dark Circle and Thousand Cuts.
Some joke summons from Summerset Isles have left the realm's magic (Summon Tolfdir, Hero of Sheo Charles, Baby Daedric Table, the mimics, Slug).

sections.heading: Wildlife
items: A bug made every forest predator spot in Skyrim a bear. Each spot now holds its own creature (skeever, wolf, spider or bear), and the Rift has about a seventh of the bears it had.
Dangerous predators (bears, sabre cats, ice wraiths, trolls) keep their distance from each other and take an hour to return once killed.
Bears still hit as hard as ever: the Rift is bear country, just not every few steps.

title: Who may vote in hold elections

sections.heading: Elections
items: To vote for a Jarl, your Discord account must be at least 90 days old, you need 10 hours of play on at least 3 different days, and your character must have been a citizen of the hold for 7 days. All three are judged when the vote opens; the hold's Voting tab tells you which one you are missing and when you will meet it.
Only those who may vote count toward the 15 citizens a hold needs to start an election.
Staff can strike a vote, with a reason, when one person has voted from more than one account, and can undo it. If your vote is struck you are told, at once or the next time you log in.
An election already running keeps the old rules, and votes already cast stand.
Citizenship began on 16 October, so no hold can start an election before about 23 October.

sections.heading: Staff
items: The Lore Master can now manage every faction from the faction panel (F3) like a Lead GM: add and remove members, name leaders and edit ranks.

sections.heading: Elections
items: A player votes in one hold only: the hold where their account first votes. Other characters on the same account can't vote in another hold's election, even if they are citizens there.

sections.heading: New
items: Solitude's eastern harbor, from the East Empire Company warehouse to the Dainty Sload, is now its own fief: Underarch Harbor, with its houses, farms, smithy, inn and chapel. The Jarl of Haafingar can grant it, and its holder is styled Harbormaster. Solitude keeps the city, Katla's Farm and the western docks.

sections.heading: Taxes and treasuries
items: Every hold and county now taxes between 10% and 40%. A Jarl, Count or Steward can no longer set the tax to 0%, and a rate that was never set counts as 10%.
Treasury gold now comes only from taxes. The weekly stipends from the Aldmeri Dominion and the Empire have ended.
New characters start with no gold, only their clothes and their tools.

sections.heading: Client 0.3.102
items: Fixed: after some logins you couldn't see people or use doors. The world now starts showing about a second into play.
Character select waits a moment until the game is ready before Play works.
The game no longer closes without a crash report when a script error happens.
The mouse pointer comes back when a message or fade closes over an open panel.
If your pack changes while a chest, barter or gift window is open, the window closes so you always see what you carry.
Spells and favourites restore reliably after login.
The map no longer shows places you've only seen as visited. Places you entered before this update show as seen until you visit them again.
Gear that ends up on a werewolf or Vampire Lord, like the arrows on its back, comes off again.
The faction panel's Realm map now has a Cyrodiil and Skyrim switch, with Skyrim's own map and its holds, towns, forts and strongholds.

sections.heading: Changes
items: The journal's World page now shows how many people are about in the world, without naming them.
/players is no longer a player command: you find out who is about by meeting them.

sections.heading: Changes
items: Equilibrium is held back for a short while for a fix. If you know it, it stays in your spellbook; you can prepare it again at a college once it returns.

sections.heading: Mining and crafting
items: The zinc, mithril and amber veins in Skyrim can now be mined. They used to say "You do not know what to do with this seam".
Zinc opens to an Apprentice Miner, mithril to an Expert Miner and amber to a Master Miner. Smelt them at any smelter.
Skinning and loom messages now read "An Apprentice" and "An Adept" instead of "A Apprentice".

sections.heading: Master Scholars write spell tomes
items: A Master Scholar can now write a spell tome of a spell they know, at a Scholars' Ledger: choose Write a spell tome.
Novice tomes need no scrolls. Apprentice tomes need 1 scroll of the same spell, Adept 2, Expert 4 and Master 5; the scrolls are used up.
A Master tome also needs a Master mage of that school who knows the spell, standing beside you and agreeing to help.
Each rank has its own wait after a tome is written: a day for Novice, 2 days for Apprentice, 4 for Adept, a week for Expert and two weeks for Master.
Tomes of raising the dead and of calling or banishing Daedra can only be written by senior college ranks.

title: Skyrim's towns, the Snow Elven Arsenal and more

sections.heading: The world
items: Skyrim's towns now work like Bruma: the people and animals that came with the mods are gone, so every NPC you meet is the server's own. Enemies and wildlife come from the server's spawns.
The College of Winterhold's main gate opens again.
Carrots can be picked again.
Falkreath is back to the Cities of the North layout: the extra JK's and Great City objects that clashed with it are gone, and its ground and navigation match again.
The Riften bank and the area by Riften's north gate are tidied up.

sections.heading: Smithing
items: The Snow Elven Arsenal: Snow Elf smiths can forge the Scout, Noble and Heavy sets and their weapons and arrows (Glass, Ebony and Elven smithing). Anyone can temper them. The Ancient One's gear is staff-only.
Black Bear Ancient Nord armour now carries its new ratings in the game files too.

sections.heading: Guilds
items: A guild's leader now holds their guild's hall, and it doesn't count toward the one-property limit. Castle Bruma is recognised as the County's, and an unowned hall goes to its faction's leader.

title: Spell picks and Grand Champion rerolls

sections.heading: Changes
items: When your magic reaches a new spell pick out in the world, the choice now opens on screen straight away instead of only a chat line. It doesn't take your keyboard, so you can finish a fight first; your journal (F3), Study Magic shelves, Scholars' Ledgers and your next login still offer it.
Grand Champion supporters get 2 identity rerolls on every character (was 1). Rerolls already used are kept, so a character that used one has one more.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Reading as a Scholar no longer finds Transmute tomes. Transmute was taken out of the game, so those tomes could not be read. You now get a tome you can actually learn.

title: Meat, Dead Man's Drink and the day of the week

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Chickens, hares, rats and dogs give their meat when you search the body again, without skinning them. Every other animal still gives its hide or part to a skinner.
Dead Man's Drink in Falkreath shows its name on the door again and counts as a building for property.
/time and the journal now name the day of the week (Sundas to Loredas), from the same clock as the sky and the moons.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Once a blocker's stamina is gone, their guard breaks every time: every blow lands in full until they have stamina again. That goes for bandits and other NPCs too.
A vampire's silver is no longer sent to the mailbox while a chest is still open. Silver you put back stays in the chest; only silver you walk off with goes to your mailbox.

title: A free identity change for the Skyrim move

sections.heading: Characters
items: Every character made before today's Skyrim update gets one free identity change: race, face, body and name. Type /reroll to use it. Your skills, gear and progress stay.
It is spent before any Patreon reroll and is open until 30 October. Yokudan armour also now counts at its tier, and Dwarven Sphere and Soul Cairn arrows no longer turn up in loot.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Gold and coin piles lying in banks, shops and homes are set dressing now and can't be picked up. Gold a player drops can still be picked up.
Dying in Blackreach, Shadowgreen Cavern or Alftand no longer sends you back to Bruma: you wake at the nearest temple.
Sun-Hallowed and Blood-Cursed Elven Arrows no longer turn up in dungeon loot.

sections.heading: Smithing
items: Ancient Imperial armour is no longer Imperial-only: any smith who has learned Schematics: Ancient Imperial can make it. The schematic is found by reading in Cyrodiil's forts, or very rarely in their chests. It is the only way to learn the craft, for Imperials too.
Black Bear Ancient Nord armour now counts at its tier: the light pieces match Scaled armour and the heavy cuirass counts 41.
Knight-Errant and Gryphon Rider armour stay Breton-only: they belong to High Rock's knightly orders.
Staff can now place a Blacksmith's Ledger at any forge that lacks one.

title: Every wild animal can be skinned

sections.heading: Skinning
items: Every wild creature can now be skinned. Animals without a pelt give their own part instead: mudcrabs their chitin, skeevers their tail, spiders their venom, trolls their fat, chaurus their chitin, horkers and mammoths their tusks, slaughterfish their scales, ice wraiths their teeth, wisps their wrappings or glow dust, netch their leather or jelly, and hares, chickens, rats and dogs their meat.
The part comes from skinning now, not from searching the body. Anything else the animal carried is still on the body.
Small parts and meat can be skinned by anyone. Prized parts need a trained Skinner, as rare pelts do: a mammoth's tusk takes a Master.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: A gate worked by a lever (such as Bruma Castle's) now comes down again when the lever is pulled a second time. It used to open once and stay up.

title: Respawns in Dawnstar, Morthal and Winterhold

sections.heading: Death
items: If you fall in Dawnstar or Morthal, you now wake by the town's Shrine of Arkay and its graves, not in another city.
If you fall in Winterhold, you now wake at Winterhold's own temple, beside the Hall of the Dead.

sections.heading: Changes
items: Some of the Daedric cults now keep a hidden place of their own. Members will know where.
Skyrim's holds, towns, forts and Orc strongholds are now recorded as lands of the realm, each held by its Jarl or its clan, ready for the day wars come to Skyrim. Nothing changes in play yet.

sections.heading: Changes
items: Skyrim's factions now own their usual halls: the Companions in Jorrvaskr, the College of Winterhold, the Bards College, the Vigil of Stendarr's Hall of the Vigilant, the Stormcloaks in the Palace of the Kings, the Dawnguard at Fort Dawnguard, Clan Volkihar's castle, the Silver Hand at Driftshade Refuge and the Nightingales at the Twilight Sepulcher.

Each hold's Jarl holds their seat (Dragonsreach, Mistveil Keep, the Blue Palace, the Palace of the Kings, Understone Keep, Highmoon Hall, the White Hall and the Jarls' longhouses), and each Orc clan its chief's longhouse.
The Thalmor now keep their own embassy in Bruma, near Fort Caractacus.
A faction's hall is where its strongbox, teaching lecterns and Scholars' Ledger work for that faction.

sections.heading: Skyrim is open
items: Skyrim is open to everyone, alongside Bruma. Solstheim, Hammerfell, Summerset, Murkmire and the other far lands stay closed for now; boats and roads that lead there will not take you.

After you make a new character you are asked where to begin: Cyrodiil (the Pale Pass road down to Bruma) or Skyrim. If you close the question it comes back a minute later. Choosing Skyrim, or walking through a hold gate, keeps you in the Realm to pick one of the nine hold gates: Whiterun, Solitude, Windhelm, Riften, Markarth, Falkreath, Morthal, Dawnstar and Winterhold.
Each gate now lands you on clear ground near its city, and Solitude, Markarth, Morthal and Dawnstar land in better places than before.

The bandits, wild animals and monsters the old world placed around the gates and inside the towns are gone; the server places Skyrim's creatures and enemies itself. Guards, townsfolk, merchants and children stay where they live.

Skyrim's lands are a big download. Updating an install you already have fetches about 16 GB of new mods and needs about 40 GB more free space; a new install downloads about 33 GB and needs about 100 GB free. The launcher does it for you before you can join.

sections.heading: New peoples
items: Snow Elf: 50% frost resistance, +15% Arcane experience. Racial power Glacier Fall: your frost damage is 25% stronger for 60 seconds.

Goblin: 50% poison resistance, +15% Gatherer experience. Racial power Feeding Frenzy: harder melee blows and faster stamina for 60 seconds. Goblins are male only, and their colour is chosen from their skin tones.
Reachman: Mongrel Blood gives 15% magic resistance and 25% poison resistance, +15% Alchemist experience. Racial power Fury of the Reach: faster stamina and magicka for 60 seconds.
Snow Elves, Goblins and Reachmen can become vampires. A Goblin vampire's thirst shows in the colour of its skin.

sections.heading: Levels
items: Each character level now gives +25 points, up from +10. Points you already have are counted again at the new rate the next time you log in.

sections.heading: Crafting
items: Each people's own armoury is made only by that people, anywhere: Yoku gear by Redguards, Apex and Lunar Guard by Khajiit, Black Bear and Steelheart by Nords, Ancient Imperial by Imperials, Gryphon Knight, Knight-Errant and Flora Druid by Bretons, Seascale by Maormer, Ancient Argonian by Argonians, crude Gild arms and Goblin armour by Goblins, and Pig Iron by Orcs. Anyone may temper them.
Yokudan, Black Bear and Apex Khajiit smithing is known by birth: those smiths need no book or teacher, only the craft tier.
The new Ancient Imperial armour counts as Ancient Imperial smithing.
Adamantium armour can be forged by every people.
The Civil War battlemage sets are faction gear for the Legion, the Stormcloaks and the Thalmor: light armour as strong as Glass, made by the faction's own smiths.
The Black Bear light hoods can be forged again.
The Dwemer Mantis armour is never forged; Game Masters give it out. The gold bars in the bank vaults are decoration and cannot be taken or smelted.

sections.heading: Alchemy
items: Every Alchemist tier brews a stronger potion. Restore potions now give back a share of your own health, stamina or magicka, from 20% up to 75%; the two strongest restore over five seconds.

Some effects open with rank: cures and Waterbreathing at Apprentice, fortify potions and Invisibility at Adept, Paralysis at Expert. Fortify Smithing, Enchanting and Illusion are no longer brewed. A locked effect falls back to the next one the mix shares and tells you why.

Fortify potions now work in fights: weapon damage, Destruction and Restoration, block, armour, lockpicking and more. Fortify Health gives extra health while it lasts. Resist Fire, Frost and Shock potions now protect you.
New special brews: Fortify Blade and Fortify Blunt (three ingredients each, from Adept), and the Blood Potion at Master, which feeds a vampire.
Alchemy and cooking experience now follow the value of what you put in. Butter, flour, milk, cheese, honey and coffee turn up in dungeons and camps, and placed foods can be gathered.

sections.heading: Blackreach
items: Blackreach is an open dungeon under Skyrim, and very hard: its Falmer, Dwemer machines, chaurus, spiders, trolls and giants shrug off a quarter of your damage. They come back 20 minutes after they fall, their bosses after 30.

Ten guarded chests stand in Blackreach. Defeat a chest's guards (its boss, if it has one) with your party, and within the hour the chest gives you one roll every 20 hours: Glass, Amber, Dwarven and honed Falmer gear among it, never Ebony, Daedric, Stalhrim or dragon materials.

sections.heading: Changes
items: Priest now trains at the normal rate, like every other skill (it had a 25% bonus). The bonus came before Priest Studies at the temples and sermons, which now give Priest more ways to train than any other skill. Levels already earned are kept.

sections.heading: Changes
items: Voice: voice range is now handled by the server. How you talk and hear does not change.
Chat, HUD and menus: the in-game overlay no longer redraws while it is hidden, so it uses less of your PC. If chat or the HUD looks old or blank after you close a menu, please tell us in #bugs.

Login: the game now loads races, head parts and face textures from our own mods correctly when you log in. Maormer faces should now come back after a relog, and a rare crash at login should be gone. If not, please tell us in #bugs with the time.
The update is about 23 MB.

sections.heading: Potion strength
items: A new Alchemist was brewing the strongest Invisibility potion (50 seconds) and the strongest Fortify Stamina potion, as if they were a Master. Each now brews the strength their Alchemist tier allows; the strongest come only at the top tiers. Potions already brewed are unchanged.

sections.heading: Combat
items: An arrow or bolt that hits your raised shield no longer hurts you. Once your guard is broken, it lands in full.
Enemies who block your blows now spend stamina doing it, as players do. With no stamina left their guard breaks, and your blows land in full.

sections.heading: Homes
items: Handing a house to another player now needs them to be a citizen of the hold it stands in, as buying one does. The hold's officials and staff can still grant houses as before.
With the Key Ring, locking a door or chest now tells you "Locked: only key holders can enter." You, and anyone with a key, still go through.

sections.heading: The world
items: New characters now start at one of 18 spots in the character creation area instead of all on one, so people making a character at the same time no longer stand inside each other.
The carrot plants at Aleswell can be picked again.

sections.heading: Skills
items: The Scholar skill's tier list now says which spell tomes each tier can find by reading: Apprentice tomes from the second tier, Adept from the third, and Expert and, very rarely, Master tomes for senior college ranks.

sections.heading: Safety and privacy
items: Behind-the-scenes security and privacy improvements to the game server.

sections.heading: Reading schematics
items: A Blacksmith no longer needs the Scholar skill to learn a schematic. Your Blacksmith craft tier alone decides which schematics you can follow.
Only a Blacksmith can learn a schematic. A Scholar who is no smith can still find schematics while reading, and sell or trade them.
Copying schematics at the Scholars' Ledger is unchanged.

sections.heading: Changes
items: Arcane Mastery: your Magic tab marks the next spell in each of your lines, and has Leave and Release buttons for an apprenticeship.
Smoother play around other players and NPCs: the game does less work for every character it draws.
Staff who are invisible can no longer be heard by players nearby.

title: Staff permissions for courts and citizenship

sections.heading: Staff
items: Only a Lead GM or above can now seat or remove officials from the F3 Court tab, or grant, decline and set the rules and fee for a hold's citizenship; a GM who holds an office (a Jarl, Count or Steward) keeps exactly that office's rights.

title: Arcane Mastery: rank spells and apprenticeship

sections.heading: Rank spells
items: After your first spell, you choose one more spell of your school at 25 (an Apprentice spell) and another at 50 (an Adept spell). Your school stops rising at 25 and at 50 until you choose. Choose in your F3 Journal's Magic tab, at a Study Magic shelf or at a Scholars' Ledger. Priest works the same way for Restoration.
Spell lines: the next spell of a line you already know is listed first, for example "Next in your line: Firebolt (from Flames)". Choosing it adds the new spell; you keep the old one.
Mages already past 25 or 50 are offered their picks too, and lose nothing.

sections.heading: Apprenticeship
items: A mage with Arcane Arts 75 (or Priest 75, for Restoration) can take another player as apprentice: open the X menu on them and choose Take as apprentice, then pick a spell. The apprentice must accept.

While near their teacher, the apprentice can cast that spell. Each cast counts as study, up to 20 a day. After about 1 day of study for a Novice spell, 2 for Apprentice, 3 for Adept, 5 for Expert and 15 for Master, the spell is theirs for good. Away from the teacher, or with the teacher gone, the spell is set aside until they return.

A teacher has one apprentice at a time. Leaders and officers of the Synod, the College of Winterhold, the College of Whispers and House Telvanni can have three. Either of you can end it from the X menu.

title: Client 0.3.97: citizenship and the first Jarl elections

sections.heading: New
items: Citizenship of the holds: notice boards have Citizenship and Voting tabs, and your F3 Journal has a Citizen tab.
Buying a house now needs citizenship of the hold it stands in. Property tax is a fixed amount, set from the property's listed value.

The first Jarl elections: once a hold of Skyrim has 15 citizens, an election opens at its notice boards, with a day to stand for Jarl and a day to vote. Bruma has no election: the Count holds the seat.

Controller support: in panels the right stick moves a pointer, A clicks, B closes and the left stick scrolls. New shortcuts: Back+LB opens skills, Back+right stick click the personal menu, Back+left stick click the emote wheel.
Citizens get their hold's Citizen role on our Discord, given and taken with your citizenship in game (it follows your character when you play).

Election notices: when a hold reaches 15 citizens, its citizens are told in game, when they next log in and on Discord that courts may be put forward, and again when the vote opens a day later, for a revote and for the result. Those who stand in a court on the ballot (the Jarl candidate, Steward, Lord Commander and Housecarl) do not vote.

sections.heading: Tailoring
items: What a loom will make is now set garment by garment rather than by what the garment is worth. Rags, work clothes and footwraps stay Novice work; robes and fur accessories are Adept; fine and noble clothes are Expert; the Emperor's Robes and a master's robes are Master work.
Bags follow the same ladder: pouches at Apprentice, satchels at Adept, backpacks at Expert.
Anything not yet placed by hand is unchanged and still goes by its value, so most recipes sit where they did.

sections.heading: Lycanthropy
items: A werewolf's bite now carries Sanies Lupinus twice as often. The disease is still rare, and a vampire's hit is still the likelier of the two.
Nothing else about the turning has changed: the fever takes the same time to peak, and Hircine's Hunt is unchanged.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: Voice: your microphone no longer stays open when you have let go of the talk key or nothing is pressed.
The beheading at the chopping block now plays for everyone near, and the headsman stands up afterwards instead of staying stuck at the block.
Dead hawks no longer pile up: their bodies fade after a few minutes.
The dead hawks on Bruma's walls can be looted.
Orc smiths now see the Orcish recipes at the forge as soon as they can make them, and steel, scaled and glass recipes appear when your Blacksmith tier allows them.
Breaking down books no longer takes smithing schematics or spell tomes.
Breaking things down now opens the item first: break one, break all, and see what it's worth, so a fast click can't take the wrong item.
Kills by your summons now count for your hunting contracts.
The carrots at Aleswell can be picked again.

Vampires: a newly turned vampire's tab now says "Not fed yet" and explains that your eyes and colour show until your first taste of blood (food doesn't count). A new "Your look" line shows whether you pass for mortal.

sections.heading: Spell tomes from reading
items: The spell tomes a Scholar finds while reading now follow the Scholar level: Apprentice tomes from 25, Adept tomes from 50, and Expert tomes from 75 for senior ranks of the Synod, the Colleges and the Great Faiths.
You no longer need a college to find Adept tomes by reading. Anyone can, from Scholar 50.
At Scholar 100, a senior college rank may very rarely find a Master spell tome.
Learning a tome still needs its school of magic at a high enough level, as before.

sections.heading: Making a character
items: Two people making a character at the same time could end up standing inside each other, with the editor's camera showing the other person instead of your own changes. Each new character is now moved to a spot of their own, and moved again if that did not take, before the editor opens.

sections.heading: Werewolves
items: Werewolves no longer stay looking like naked humans to other players. Anyone still seen that way shows their true form again at their next change.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: No more cloned, floating players: other players' characters are built once and stay dressed and on the ground.
Fewer crashes when other players come into view (their faces are rebuilt once, not every time they reappear).

sections.heading: New
items: The Key Ring panel: open it from the Keys tab in your F3 Journal, the Key Ring button in a property menu, or Give a key on another player.
Khajiit can use Night Eye from the racial power box in the F3 Journal: 60 seconds of night vision, every 20 minutes.
Watchers now see the beheading at the chopping block.

sections.heading: Back from 0.3.95
items: Changes to your RaceMenu sliders save from /appearance too, and your face no longer changes when you log back in.
Salt, Aversion poisons and Waterbreathing potions can be stored and dropped again.
Notice boards have Supply orders and Couriers buttons.

Your Other Player Volume is kept between game starts; no name tag shows over someone under Invisibility; a second character no longer inherits the first one's enchantments; staff keep their Admin chat tab.

sections.heading: Executions
items: The chopping block before Castle Bruma can now be used: press E at it.

sections.heading: Colleges and classes
items: Classes at the Class Lectern are now held by a college's leader and officers (the Arch-Mage, Master Wizards, the Chancellor, Magisters, the Master of Whispers, Keepers of Secrets); staff no longer name teachers.
An Apprentice in a Novice class now takes half the lesson (was 35%).

sections.heading: Notice boards
items: Notices pinned while wearing a mask are now signed with your own name.

sections.heading: The Key Ring
items: House keys are no longer items you carry: every key is kept on your key ring, so copies never stack or get mixed up. Type /keys to see yours in a menu.
Give a key on another player's menu (X) hands one of your keys to them. They accept or decline it in a menu.
Owners see every copy of their locks and who holds it in /keys, can cut a new key there, and can take a single copy back. A key taken back stops working.
Keys you carry move onto your key ring the next time you log in. Keys left in a chest or sack move onto the ring of whoever opens it next.
Since keys are no longer items, they are not dropped or stored any more.

sections.heading: House keys fixed
items: Keys cut since 8 October open their doors again and move onto your key ring when you log in (they had stopped working after this morning's update).

sections.heading: Fixes since the update
items: Vampires and werewolves keep Quicksilver ore and ingots again: they were mailed away as if they were silver. Other things that only have silver in the name stay too, such as the Silver-Blood ring and keys, house keys and Silver Hand armour. Real silver is still shunned.
Executions: once the headsman confirms, the execution happens. Standing up, walking away or logging out during the swing no longer stops it.
Executions: the GM who allows an execution must stay at the block until the headsman confirms, or there is no execution.
Executions: a GM can no longer approve an execution they take part in, as the headsman or at the block. Another GM must decide.

sections.heading: Executions at Castle Bruma
items: A chopping block now stands on the plaza before Castle Bruma. The condemned kneels at the block, and a headsman takes up the axe.
An execution needs a GM present to approve it, and the headsman confirms before the blow. A beheading ends the condemned character for good.
If the condemned or the headsman steps away, or nobody approves in time, there is no execution.

sections.heading: Silver and the cursed
items: A vampire or werewolf can no longer carry silver, not only wear it. Silver weapons, jewellery, ingots and ore in their pack are sent to their own mailbox at the notice boards, so nothing is lost; picking it up again sends it straight back.

sections.heading: Soul Trap
items: A Soul Trap weapon with no charge left no longer fills soul gems.
Capturing a soul with Soul Trap now trains Enchanting a little (up to 10 souls an hour).

sections.heading: Combat
items: Blocking an NPC's blow now costs stamina, as it does against players, and your guard breaks when your stamina runs out.

sections.heading: Unstuck
items: /unstuck now has a 30 minute wait between uses, and it cannot be used during a fight with anyone, creatures included. Wait a minute after the last blow.

sections.heading: House keys
items: House keys are no longer all "Werewolf Cage Keys": each lock now has its own key, named for its house. Your keys change over the next time you log in, and keys you hold no longer vanish and come back every few seconds.
Single keys can now be traded and stored on their own.
House keys can be dropped. A dropped key disappears after 2 minutes, but until then whoever picks it up can open that door, so keep them safe.
A key that no longer opens anything stays a Werewolf Cage Key. Keys left in a chest change over once they are taken out and their holder logs in again.

sections.heading: Property
items: Every house, room and chest bought before per-character ownership now belongs to one character, so your other characters on the same account no longer share it.

sections.heading: Supply orders
items: An order is filled by any item of the name it asks for: the woodcutters' Charcoal now fills a Charcoal order.

sections.heading: Colleges and classes
items: The Cathedral's tome shop is named for the Great Faiths, not the Synod.
Staff can now name class teachers straight from the player menu, so Class Lecterns can be opened to the colleges' teachers. Ask a GM if you are ready to teach a class.

sections.heading: Skills
items: When your work stops counting towards a skill, you are now told why and for how long.
The /teach hint names the rank you actually need.

sections.heading: Faction gear
items: The whole Vigil of Stendarr set now belongs to the Vigil alone.

sections.heading: Loot
items: No giant's club drops as loot any more.

sections.heading: Staff
items: Trial GMs now have the admin panel's Ghost mode and Teleport tab.

title: Giant's clubs withdrawn, teaching, privacy and mining fixes

sections.heading: Giant's clubs withdrawn
items: Giant's clubs were far too strong in players' hands and can no longer be forged or improved. Every club, in your pack or in a chest, is exchanged for a Steel Warhammer. If your club was taken earlier today with its materials refunded, you keep the materials and get a Steel Warhammer as well.

sections.heading: Teaching and the halls
items: Teaching a spell at a faction's Scholars' Ledger or Class Lectern works again at the Cathedral of St Martin, the Synod Conclave and Frostcrag Spire. Priests and up teach Restoration and Alteration at the Cathedral's ledger, Senior Magisters at the Synod's ledger and Class Lectern, and Senior Whisperers at Frostcrag Spire. The College of Winterhold is not covered yet.
Spell tomes bought at the Cathedral now show the Great Faiths' name and pay into their treasury.

sections.heading: Privacy
items: The Court roster and other lists (factions, nobility, party, ledger, pigeon contacts, letters and more) no longer show "Werewolf" or "Vampire Lord" for someone in beast form.
Typing a name no longer finds someone in beast form or behind a mask; use their #TAG.
Standing near someone masked or in beast form no longer adds them to your ledger or pigeon contacts.

sections.heading: Mining and smelting
items: Four iron-looking veins in Frost-Iron Mine hold quicksilver. They now say so, and which Miner rank opens them, instead of only "Quicksilver is beyond your skill".
A Quicksilver Ingot now costs 2 charcoal, as announced on 7 October.

sections.heading: Logging in
items: If your game loads into the wrong place at login (for example Riverwood's Sleeping Giant Inn), the server now keeps your outfit and favourites, puts you back where you were and tells you to restart your game.

sections.heading: Staff
items: The Admin chat tab now appears reliably for staff after a reconnect or character switch.
Several waiting GM calls are now reminded in one line instead of one line each.
Trial GMs now have the Admin chat tab and /admin, so they see GM call alerts.

sections.heading: Appearance
items: Changes made with the RaceMenu sliders (face shape, expressions, sizes, body and overlays) when creating a character are now saved and shown to other players, and they stay after a relog. Saving slider changes from /appearance on an existing character is still being fixed.

sections.heading: Relaunch through the launcher
items: This update brings client 0.3.94: relaunch through the launcher to get it. You will be asked to accept the updated Terms and Privacy Policy once if you have not yet.

sections.heading: Every blessing in Active Effects
items: Every blessing now shows under Active Effects, including those of Sanguine, Hermaeus Mora, the Hist, the Ancestors, the Yokudan Gods and Ithelia.

sections.heading: A new faith: Ithelia
items: A new faith: Ithelia, the Daedric Prince of Paths, once erased from memory. Her followers pray to her anywhere; there is no shrine. Her blessing keeps them on the road: stamina returns 50% faster.

sections.heading: Fewer chat commands: everything from a panel: Every command in one place
items: Press U, or type / on its own in chat, to open every command you can use. Search it by a word or two: party, bank, pigeon, bug.

Commands that need more than a click now ask for it on the panel: a choice of words, a box for a number or a message, and a list of the people you know to pick a name from. The panel shows the exact line it will send before you run it.
Staff see every staff command they may use there too, by topic.

sections.heading: Fewer chat commands: everything from a panel: Buttons where you need them
items: At a shrine of your own god, leave an offering from the shrine's panel.
In the pigeon coop: ignore whoever sent a letter, without learning who it was, and choose how your next letter is signed.
Found a faction from the Faction panel while charters are open.
Your journal (F3) has a new World page: who is about, who rules, what is open, the time, named beasts and wildlife. Its Profile page can start an identity reroll and open a ticket with staff.
With your hands bound, press U to struggle.
Using an Arcane Enchanter now brings back every enchantment you have learned by itself; /syncenchant is no longer needed.

sections.heading: The Court tab
items: The Court tab (F3) now sets the hold's tax rate and each office's weekly wage.

sections.heading: Buying a house
items: Houses can be bought: a hold's Count or Steward puts an empty house up for sale from its door's property menu, and the first to pay the price owns it. The gold goes to the hold's treasury. Renting moved into the same panel.

You pay the price the panel showed you. If an official changes the price while your panel is open, nothing is paid and the panel shows the new price. From chat, say /property buy <price> at the door to buy it at the price you name.
A bought house pays the weekly property tax on its sale price. A sale far below the house's value halves its tax value at most, so a house sold for a token price is not taxed on that price.
Houses can be sold only in a hold that keeps a treasury.

sections.heading: The nobility of Bruma
items: The County of Bruma is divided into fiefs: the towns of Applewatch, Aleswell, Greenwood and Mountain Watch. The Count or Countess of Bruma, and nobody else, grants and takes back titles: a Baron or Baroness holds a fief, a Lord or Lady an estate, and a Knight or Dame an honour. Every grant and every revocation is proclaimed by decree.

A Baron or Baroness looks after the houses of their own town as a steward does: granting a house, taking it back, assigning its rooms and chests, renting houses out and setting their value for tax. Their own houses in their town do not count against the one-house limit. They have no say outside it, and no seat at the court.
A quarter of the weekly property tax on the houses of a fief goes into that fief's own treasury, which nobody can take gold out of. The rest goes to the County as before.

Your journal (F3) has a Nobility tab: everyone sees the county's roll of nobles and its fiefs; a noble sees their title, their fief's houses and its treasury; the ruler grants and revokes titles there.
Lord Elion, who bought Mountain Watch from the Countess, is its Baron.

sections.heading: Racial powers: Racial Powers
items: Every race now has a Racial Power, called once a real day from the Profile tab of your journal (F3). Waiting out the day survives a relog.

Altmer, Highborn: magicka regenerates 50% faster for 60 seconds. Argonian, Histskin: health regenerates 50% faster and physical blows do 15% less for 60 seconds. Bosmer, Wild Hunt: bows deal 20% more and stamina regenerates 50% faster for 30 seconds. Breton, Dragonskin: 25% more magic resistance for 60 seconds. Dunmer, Ancestor's Wrath: your fire deals 25% more for 60 seconds.

Imperial, Voice of the Emperor: health and stamina regenerate 50% faster for 60 seconds. Nord, Battle Cry: 15% more melee damage for 60 seconds. Orc, Berserker Rage: 25% more melee damage and 25% less damage taken for 30 seconds. Redguard, Adrenaline Rush: stamina regenerates 50% faster for 60 seconds. Maormer, Roaring Tempest: 25% more magic resistance and a ward that absorbs 60 points of spell damage for 60 seconds.
The Khajiit's Night Eye comes with a later update of the game.
However many gifts, blessings and powers you stack, no hit is ever reduced by more than 75%.

sections.heading: Racial powers: Racial gifts
items: Each race learns one skill 15% faster: Altmer and Dunmer Arcane Arts, Argonians Harvesting, Bosmer Archery, Bretons Priest, Imperials Defense, Khajiit Martial Arts, Nords, Redguards and Maormer Blade, Orcs Blacksmith. It speeds the skill up; the hourly and daily limits stay the same.
The Maormer have their own gifts instead of the Altmer's: 50% resistance to shock, and they swim faster.
Argonians: the Hist keeps out half of the curses a vampire's or werewolf's attack, or a vampire's feeding, would pass on.

sections.heading: The vampire's bite
items: When a vampire feeds on a standing player, the two now play the bite together, and everyone nearby sees it.

sections.heading: Armour for the College of Whispers
items: The College of Whispers has its own armour: Witchplate with red runes, forged by the College's Artificer.

sections.heading: The Great Faiths and the College of Whispers
items: The Great Faiths, the order of the Eight Divines at the Cathedral of St Martin in Bruma, are now a faction with ranks from Novice to High Priest. At the Cathedral's Scholars' Ledger they sell Restoration and Alteration tomes to their own members, by rank as the colleges do, and their Senior ranks (Priest and up) teach those spells there.
At the end of a sermon, everyone who stayed is offered the sermon's spell, as at a college class. You can also change your prepared spells in the Cathedral.
The College of Whispers now has its own tome shop at the Scholars' Ledger in Frostcrag Spire. Its members can still buy at the Synod Conclave too.
The Imperial Cult, the Empire's own worship of the Divines, is now a faction too. Its chapel, tome shop and teaching come later.
The Great Faiths and the Imperial Cult each count as your one guild, and their faithful cannot also serve a Daedric cult.

sections.heading: Couriers: Couriers
items: You can now hire a courier to carry goods for you. At a notice board, open the pigeon coop and choose Couriers: pick up to six kinds of goods, where they go and who receives them, and the pay you offer. The board holds the goods and the pay, and a small posting fee goes to the hold's treasury.

Goods can go to a settlement's drop point around Bruma (Aleswell, Greenwood, Mountain Watch and Applewatch), where they wait in the recipient's mailbox, or to the recipient in person: the courier finds them and offers the parcel, and they take it into their pack or have it left in their mailbox.

Anyone can take a courier job at the board where it was posted. You carry one Sealed Courier's Parcel, which cannot be dropped, stored or traded until it is delivered. Deliver it within three days of game time to be paid; if time runs out, the parcel goes back and the goods return to the sender.
Bandits beware, and couriers too: robbing a courier may take their parcel. The robber gets a Broken Courier's Parcel to open at a notice board, and the courier is not paid.

Senders can insure a parcel for up to the goods' value, for 10% of that value. If it is robbed, the hold's treasury pays the sender, as far as the treasury allows. Insurance does not pay out when the robber is the sender, the courier or the recipient, or shares a party or faction with the sender or the courier, and a sender can claim at most twice a week.

sections.heading: Couriers: Courier ranks
items: Couriers rise in rank with their deliveries. A Novice carries one parcel at a time and takes jobs worth up to 500 gold; an Apprentice (5 deliveries) two parcels and up to 1,500; a Journeyman (15) three and up to 4,000, and may carry to other holds; an Expert (40) four and up to 10,000; a Master (100) five, of any value.
The higher your rank, the less often a robbery takes your parcel: one in two for a Novice, one in four for a Master.
A delivery counts toward your rank when it pays at least 20 gold, and at most three a day count from the same sender. Your rank shows at the top of the Couriers tab.

sections.heading: Hold taxes and wages: Taxes
items: A hold's tax rate now covers property as well as rents. The rate its Count, Jarl or Steward sets (with /tax, or on the Treasury page of the faction panel, F3) is charged each Sunday on every owned house, shop and storage building on the hold's land, from the owner's bank account into the hold's treasury.
The rate is from 0% to 30%. Bruma's rate is up to its officials: it stays 0% until they set one.

sections.heading: Hold taxes and wages: Wages
items: A hold's officials and guards are now paid every Sunday, into their bank account, without having to be online: Guard 50 gold a week, Guard Captain and Court Mage 100, Steward 150, until the ruler or the Steward sets other wages on the Treasury page (F3). The ruler is never paid, and nobody sets their own wage.
Wages come from what the hold took in that week and, when that is not enough, from up to a quarter of its savings. What the treasury cannot pay is owed and paid first the next week.

sections.heading: Spells on creatures and people
items: Ash Rune's paralysis now holds creatures and NPCs in place too, not only players.
Spells that burn, freeze or drain over time now deal their full damage to creatures and NPCs.
Slows and staggers from spells now reach creatures and NPCs reliably, wear off properly, and stay on when another player's game takes over the creature.

sections.heading: Masks, beast forms and a freeze
items: Logging out in Beast Form while wearing a mask no longer loses your character's name. Before, the character came back named "Masked Person" for good. If this happened to you, open a ticket and staff will put your name back.
Fixed a freeze of the whole server, up to 30 seconds, when someone made a new character soon after a restart.

sections.heading: Your map remembers
items: Discovered map locations are now saved on the server for each character, so they stay after a logout, a game repair or on another PC.

sections.heading: Locked storage
items: A chest you claim now starts locked. Claimed chests that had been left open outside a place were locked once; their owners can unlock them again from the menu.

sections.heading: Report a GM
items: Discord tickets have a new Report a GM button. Only the server owners can read these tickets.

sections.heading: Tailor ranks at the loom
items: Tailor ranks now count at the loom: Fine clothes need an Apprentice Tailor, Noble an Adept, Scaled an Expert and Masterwork a Master.

sections.heading: First person after a beast form
items: First person works again after you change back from a werewolf or Vampire Lord.

sections.heading: Holding a skill
items: Hold now means a skill neither rises nor falls. If you set a skill to Hold to protect it and still want to train it, set it to Raise in your skills (K).
While you train a held skill you are reminded once an hour, and reading or study refuses to raise it.

sections.heading: Command Daedra and the Ash Guardian
items: Command Daedra can now take control of another player's summoned daedra for the spell's duration, where the PvP rules allow it.
Conjure Ash Guardian now raises a guardian that everyone can see. It guards its spot until it is destroyed.

sections.heading: Dungeon torches
items: Fixed wall torches multiplying in dungeons: every server restart added another torch to each sconce, up to 57 on one wall (the bright bulbs, the roaring fire sound and the lag in Red Ruby Cave, Bruma Caverns, Fort Cutpurse and others).

sections.heading: Voices carry better
items: Voices carry better: someone talking is at full volume out to about 5 metres, and you can turn a single person up to 400%.

sections.heading: Vampires fear fire
items: Vampire creatures and NPCs now take 50% more damage from fire and 25% more from silver. Before, only vampire players had these weaknesses.

sections.heading: Force Rune pushes
items: Force Rune now throws back the player it catches, as it should, instead of only making them stagger. Creatures and NPCs it catches are thrown back too once every player has the next client update.

sections.heading: Guard armour
items: Only Bruma's guard armour can be forged in Cyrodiil for now. The guard armour of Anvil, Bravil, Cheydinhal, Chorrol, Kvatch, Leyawiin and Skingrad (armour, helmet, boots, gauntlets and shield) does not show in game, so whoever wore it looked invisible or bald. It can no longer be forged or improved, and your materials stay with you if you try.
None of these pieces drop as loot either. Bruma's guard armour is unchanged.
Any of these pieces already made are taken back, and whoever held one gets the materials for forging it returned (boots and gauntlets have no forging recipe, so they return nothing).

sections.heading: World and weapon fixes: Weapons
items: The Stormcloak Sword, War Axe, Bearded Axe, Greatsword and Battleaxe now have the same base damage as the other factions' weapons (12, 13, 13, 21 and 22).
The Dawnguard War Axe SPR and the Enhanced Crossbow SPR no longer deal many times the damage they should: they now have 13 and 19.

sections.heading: World and weapon fixes: Great House cloaks
items: The Rhino Beetle Cloak, the Bonesaint Cloak and the Redoran Watchman Cloak can no longer be made at the Loom or the forge. They looked the same as the Great Houses' own cloaks, which stay faction gear.

sections.heading: World and weapon fixes: The world
items: The Cathedral of St. Martin in Bruma now has a Scholars' Ledger.
Frost-Iron Mine near Mountain Watch and Bleak-Frost Mine behind Bruma each have their own entrance again: their doors no longer lead into the wrong mine.
The Bandit Ringleader who kept appearing in Silorn but could not be hurt is gone.

sections.heading: Launcher
items: A failed launcher update no longer locks the Play button, and updates retry when Windows briefly holds the file.
A game started right after closing the last one is watched for crashes too.
The top bar labels its Discord and Nexus buttons.

sections.heading: Launcher
items: Fixed "Update failed: EPERM" when the launcher updates itself. A copy of the update left over from an earlier try, often held by an antivirus scan, could block every new try.
If an update still fails, the launcher now offers a button to download it yourself. It installs over the old launcher and keeps your game files.
Already stuck on that error? Download 2.1.47 once from https://files.dragonbreakonline.com/launcher/2.1.47/DragonBreakLauncher.exe and run it. Updates after that use the fix.

sections.heading: Client
items: The emote wheel (B) opens and closes smoothly: it no longer bogs the screen down on large monitors, B now closes it, and a wheel left without a cursor closes by itself.
Sitting on a chair or bench while carrying house keys no longer causes hitches.
The key settings in the journal (F3) now say that Mouse 4 and Mouse 5 are set in the launcher's settings.

sections.heading: Client
items: Conjured Bonemen and NPC archers keep their arrows and their bows: a Boneman now draws and shoots instead of putting its bow away.
An NPC's weapon that shows as equipped but isn't in its hand is put back in its hand.

sections.heading: Pigeon post
items: A pigeon letter can now carry gold, but no goods. Goods will travel with player couriers, coming soon. Parcels already on their way can still be collected at any notice board.

title: Fixes for study, copying, masks and brewing

sections.heading: Server
items: A pause of several seconds that froze the server about every six hours is fixed.

sections.heading: Priest Studies
items: Priest Studies now tells you when your Wheel of Skills has no room for Priest (the day's limit, the hourly limit, Priest marked to fall, or the higher places held by your other skills), instead of letting you study for nothing. A sitting that reaches one of those limits ends and says when study pays again.

sections.heading: Copying
items: Copies of manuals and schematics at the Scholars' Ledger now have their own daily count. Books you copy while reading no longer use it up, and the message tells you how many you have copied today.

sections.heading: Masks
items: Putting on a mask can no longer leave you stuck as a Masked Person. If it happened to you, send a /bug and staff will give your name back.

sections.heading: Crafting
items: Brewing potions now gets the Alchemist's craft bonus and the first-craft bonus, as intended.
A Dark Elf or Orc smith keeps a schematic for a technique they already know by birth instead of using it up.

Faction gear now tempers as far as your own Blacksmith craft tier allows, one improvement level per tier, up to Legendary. The Officer's Sword, the Penitus Oculatus Sword and the General's Sword no longer stop at Superior (or refuse to improve at all), and the same goes for every other faction piece. Other gear tempers as before.

title: Overpowered gear can no longer be forged or looted

sections.heading: Smithing
items: The Dawnguard War Axe SPR and the Enhanced Crossbow SPR can no longer be forged or improved by anyone, Dawnguard smiths included: they were far stronger than intended. Your materials stay with you if you try.
Every Dawnguard War Axe SPR already made has been removed, and the smith who forged them has been given their materials back.

The same goes for the armour of the Lost Ark Reborn Paladin Legendary set, both the normal and the Alt version (body, helm, hands, shoes and cloak): each piece gave far more protection than Daedric armour. The set's swords are unchanged.
None of these drop as loot, and neither does the frost giant's club, which hit far harder than any weapon a player should carry.

title: Spell tomes from reading follow your college rank

sections.heading: Reading
items: The higher spell tomes now belong to the colleges. The tomes you find while reading depend on your rank in the Synod, the College of Winterhold or the College of Whispers: without a college rank (and as an Initiate, smith or robe-maker) you find Novice and Apprentice tomes. Senior ranks and above can find Adept tomes too, if their Scholar skill is high enough. Master tomes never come from reading; they come only through a college.

Your chance of finding a tome is the same as before: you simply find one of the ranks you are allowed. Raising the dead and calling or banishing the Daedra stay restricted arts, so only Senior ranks and above find those tomes in books.

sections.heading: Spell tomes
items: Senior ranks and above now get one tome every 3 days instead of two a week, still shared between buying a tome and teaching a spell. Everyone else can still buy one a week.

sections.heading: Client
items: Other players and NPCs are outlined again when a glow should show on them, and a Racial Power's look (such as Roaring Tempest's shock cloak) shows to everyone nearby.
Busy areas stutter less when many NPCs appear or leave at once: the game now places them a few at a time.
Wolves around Bruma stand and fight again instead of running off; deer, foxes, hares and other prey still flee.
Werewolves and Vampire Lords can use their Shout and Sneak powers from a mouse button.

Mouse buttons for the menu keys, the back and forward buttons (Mouse 4 and Mouse 5) included, are set in the launcher's settings (launcher 2.1.46). The key settings in the journal (F3) take keyboard keys and the middle mouse button only.
Pigeon coops can send and collect parcels of gold and goods, and have a new Supply orders tab.
A new journal tab for those who serve the Dominion: Thalmor.
Switching characters no longer leaves your old character's body standing in the world.
A werewolf or vampire lord who is downed and revived wakes in their own shape.
A crash when someone near you was downed or died while talking is fixed.
A filled soul gem no longer pops its notice up over and over.
The Maormer can be made in the character creator.
The client now sends the server a short performance report every 30 seconds, so we can track down lag.

sections.heading: Items
items: Backpacks, satchels and pouches now show on your character when worn, and they add to what you can carry: a backpack +50, a satchel +25, a pouch +10. A cape can be worn with a backpack or satchel.
The Officer's Sword, the General's Sword and the Penitus Oculatus Sword now have the same base damage (12).
Zahkrii do Bormahu shows its real colours again (gold guard, dark blade, leather grip) instead of a pale glassy look.
The weapons that came on the racks in player buildings are gone, so those racks are free to hold your own.
Malacath's Band of Brutality has a new look, and its enchantment now works: it raises your armor rating by 30.

sections.heading: Maormer
items: New sea-blue and sea-green skin colours for the Maormer. New characters pick from them in the creator, and an existing Maormer can choose one of the new colours with /appearance.

sections.heading: The world
items: The carrot plant now gives carrots, not leeks.
Bruma's statue of Meridia now shows a prayer prompt. In Underpall, the low-hanging icicles that players walked into are gone.
Fingerbowl Cave has been rebuilt where its rooms were out of place, and it now has a map marker.
Scamps cast fire again.

sections.heading: Property
items: New houses, rooms and businesses now belong to the character who buys them, not to your whole account: property tax comes from that character's bank, rent and takings go to that character, and only that character (and the people holding its keys) can use it.
Each character can own one home, and each account up to two.
A faction's hall now follows the faction's current leader, whoever owns the building.
Property you already owned before this update stays shared by your whole account, as before. Only property bought from now on belongs to one character.

title: Parcels and supply orders by pigeon

sections.heading: Pigeon post
items: A pigeon letter can now carry a parcel: gold and up to six kinds of goods. The town whose board it flies from takes a tenth of the gold and 5 gold for each kind of goods. The one you send it to collects it at any notice board.

Players can post supply orders at a notice board: ask for a number of one item and set a reward. The board holds the reward, and posting costs a tenth of it (at least 10 gold). Anyone else can bring the goods to a board in the same hold and is paid at once for what they hand in, and the goods go to the poster's mailbox.
An order stays open for a week. Whatever reward is left when it ends or is cancelled goes back to the poster's mailbox; the posting fee is kept. Each account can have three orders open at once.

sections.heading: Skinning
items: Dragons can now be skinned, but only by a Master Skinner: their bones and scales come off the body through skinning. Their gold and gems can still be looted as before.

sections.heading: Reading
items: Spell tomes from reading no longer stop at two a day. They're a rare chance on every reading, rarer after each one you find that day, and still guaranteed after 100 readings without one.

sections.heading: Smithing
items: Every Dark Elf smith knows Bonemold and Chitin, and every Orc smith knows Orcish, once they reach the craft tier. Both can teach it to others.

sections.heading: Property
items: The lord of Mountain Watch now owns the chests and inner rooms of his buildings too, so he can assign them to his people.

title: Waning skills give back every point

sections.heading: Skills
items: A skill you let wane now falls all the way to 0 when it is a trade you can take up again just by doing it; skills that need a tome or a rite to open stop at 1.

sections.heading: Weapon racks
items: Weapon racks in homes now hold weapons. Hold the weapon you want to show and use an empty rack to hang it there; use the rack again to take it back. Shield racks take the shield you carry, and dagger displays take daggers.
Only a home's owner and the people holding its key can put weapons on its racks or take them down. Raiders never take weapons from a rack.

A hold's leaders (its Jarl or Count, Baron, Steward, Chieftain or Bane) can take weapons down from racks in buildings in their own hold, and they keep them. It is up to them what happens to the weapons next.
A weapon on a rack keeps its enchantment, its tempering and its name.
If a home changes hands or is given up, the weapons on its racks go back to the previous owner, at once if they are online or when they next log in.
Racks that came with a weapon on them keep it as decoration. You cannot take it, and it does not make room for one of yours.

sections.heading: Crafting skills
items: The first time you make something you have never made before, it is worth three times the usual progress toward that skill. This counts for Cook, Blacksmith, Alchemist and Tailor, each skill on its own.
The full bonus lasts for your first 25 different items in a skill, then grows smaller with each new one, so trying new recipes always pays a little more than repeating old ones.
The hourly and daily limits on each skill still apply, and tempering does not count as making something new.
The server starts keeping track with this update, so things you made before it count as new the first time you make them again.

title: Faster crafting skills, and soul gems in Bruma

sections.heading: Skills
items: Brewing potions trains Alchemist twice as fast, and cooking trains Cook twice as fast. Chopping wood and work at the lumber mill train Woodcutter one and a half times as fast. Your hourly and daily skill limits stay the same.

sections.heading: Mining
items: Three veins deep in the Bleak Mine are now Geode Veins. A miner of Apprentice rank or higher can crack one open for an empty soul gem, so enchanters no longer have to leave Bruma for soul gems.

sections.heading: Weapons
items: Two artifact swords have come into the world: Harmony and Mayhem.
A creature or NPC struck by Harmony calms down and will not fight anyone for 20 seconds. One struck by Mayhem flies into a frenzy and attacks anything near it for 20 seconds.
Striking again starts the 20 seconds over, and a strike from the other blade turns calm into frenzy or frenzy into calm.
Neither blade's effect works on other players: against adventurers they are ordinary swords.

sections.heading: Vampires
items: Vampires cannot use Restoration's healing spells, and healing magic does nothing for them. Restoration's spells against the undead still burn them.

sections.heading: The Thalmor
items: Under the White-Gold Concordat the worship of Talos is outlawed in the Empire, and the Thalmor may enforce it. In Cyrodiil (Bruma) a First Emissary, Justiciar or Inquisitor can arrest a follower of Talos: look at them, press X and choose Arrest under the Concordat. The one arrested is told why.
A Concordat arrest is lawful. At a cell door in the jail the Thalmor can pass the Concordat's sentence of 30 minutes, and only the Thalmor can let the prisoner out early; the guards will not.

In Skyrim the Thalmor have no arrest powers at all: the Holds rule themselves and the Concordat binds only the Empire. A Thalmor rank no longer lets anyone restrain or jail people in Skyrim; it works again on returning to Cyrodiil.

The Thalmor have informants. When anyone kneels at a shrine of Talos in Cyrodiil, the First Emissary, Justiciars and Inquisitors who are online hear of it: which shrine, where and when, but never who.

The Thalmor keep dossiers: notes on named characters, written by the First Emissary and Justiciars and read by Inquisitors too. The reports and dossiers are in a new Thalmor tab of the journal (F3), which only those ranks see.
The Aldmeri Dominion pays the Thalmor a stipend of 300 gold into their treasury at every weekly reckoning.

Only High Elves, Wood Elves and Khajiit (the Dominion's peoples, vampires among them) can join the Thalmor, and only High Elves can be First Emissary or Justiciar. The Maormer are the Dominion's enemies and are not taken. Nobody already in the Thalmor is removed.

sections.heading: Religion
items: The Maormer have a faith of their own: the Deep Serpents, the great sea serpents their people ride. Pray at the Serpent Stone on the lake shore north-east of Bruma for the Blessing of the Deep Serpents: water breathing and resistance to poison.

title: No faction gear in dungeon chests

sections.heading: Loot
items: Enchanted Imperial swords, bows and armour no longer turn up in dungeon chests, on bodies or in camps. They are Imperial Legion gear, made only by the Legion's smiths, like the plain Imperial pieces already were. The same goes for enchanted Vampire clan, Dawnguard and Orcish gear.

sections.heading: Magic
items: Transmute Mineral Ore has been taken out of the game, because turning iron into silver and gold broke the economy. Its tome is no longer sold and can no longer be read, and nobody can teach it. Anyone who knew it loses it the next time they log in.

title: Mages' colleges: tomes by rank, teaching and classes for beginners

sections.heading: Spell tomes
items: What a college sells you now depends on your rank. Members above Initiate (Mage of the Synod, Whisperer, Wizard, Associate, Scholar, Novice, Apprentice) can buy Novice and Apprentice tomes. Senior ranks and above (Senior Magister, Senior Whisperer, Senior Wizard and up) can buy up to Expert. Master tomes are still not sold, and Initiates and the colleges' smiths and robe-makers still buy none.
Senior ranks and above can buy one tome every 3 days. Everyone else can still buy one a week.

Raising the dead (Raise Zombie, Reanimate Corpse, Revenant, Dread Zombie, Dead Thrall, Cyrodiil's zombie spells, and Conjure Boneman, Mistman and Wrathman from the Soul Cairn) and calling the Daedra lords (Conjure Dremora Lord, the Golden Saints and Dark Seducers, Staada) are restricted arts, along with Banish, Expel and Command Daedra. Only Senior ranks and above can buy or be taught them. Senior ranks can now buy Banish Daedra at the Synod, though it is a tome of Skyrim.

sections.heading: Teaching a spell
items: A Senior rank or above can now teach a spell straight to a member of their own college, with no book needed. Use your college's Scholars' Ledger (in the Synod Conclave, or in Frostcrag Spire for the College of Whispers) or its Class Lectern, choose "Teach a spell to a student", then pick the student and the spell. The student has to be standing nearby (within 15 m) and accept.

Each lesson uses up a tome of that spell if you carry one. If you don't, it uses your tome purchase (one every 3 days for a Senior rank). The student still needs the skill and the school of magic for the spell, and is taught spells up to the rank they could buy (Apprentice at least, so Initiates can be taught their first spells too).

sections.heading: Classes
items: A mage can now hold classes at a Class Lectern with Arcane Arts at 75, as well as with Expert study in a school.

Students who have not reached their first spell yet (Arcane Arts below 25, no school chosen) can now join a Novice or Apprentice class. They learn Arcane Arts while they stay in the classroom, at about twice the pace of studying alone. The usual hourly and daily skill limits still apply.

When the teacher ends a class, everyone who stayed to the end is offered the class's spell to learn (Learn or Decline, for three minutes). The usual rules apply: you need the skill and school of magic for it, it must be within the rank you could buy, and the restricted arts are only for Senior ranks. A class's spell costs the teacher one tome of it, or their tome purchase, once for the whole class.

sections.heading: Schools of magic
items: Casting a Conjuration spell now counts twice as much toward your study of Conjuration, since a summon is cast far less often than a bolt.

title: The tome shelf favours your school

sections.heading: Magic
items: The weekly spell tome shelf at the Scholars' Ledger now puts tomes of your primary school of magic first. Three of its four places go to your primary school, and the last goes to your secondary school or Restoration when the shelf has one you can learn.

title: Legion swords join the faction balance

sections.heading: Factions
items: The Officer's Sword, the General's Sword and the Penitus Oculatus Sword now get the same damage bonus as the other faction weapons (a Glass weapon's). All three now have the same base damage too (12).
Only smiths of the Imperial Legion can forge the Officer's Sword and the General's Sword. The Penitus Oculatus Sword is made by smiths of the Penitus Oculatus or the Legion.

title: The Great Hunt waits for the whole account

sections.heading: Shrines
items: The wait after running the Great Hunt, or after failing a rite at Hircine's or Molag Bal's shrine, now counts for all your characters, not just the one who ran it. Making a new character no longer skips it.
Waits already running on any of your characters count too.

sections.heading: Loot
items: Torches are now a rare find in dungeon and expedition chests, and a chest holds one at most. Torches you find lying in the world can still be picked up as before.

title: Looking into items bouncing out of chests

sections.heading: Containers
items: Some of you have seen items put into a barrel or chest jump back out. For the next day the server keeps a short record of items put into containers so we can find the cause. Nothing changes in play.

title: Study Magic tells you when it cannot pay

sections.heading: Magic
items: Before your first spell, Study Magic trains Arcane Arts within your skill limits for the hour and the day. If you have reached a limit, the shelf now tells you before you sit down and says when study pays again. If you reach a limit while you are studying, the sitting ends and tells you why. Before, you could study for twenty minutes and gain nothing.

title: Lock spells at their proper rank

sections.heading: Magic
items: The Open Expert Lock and Open Master Lock tomes are now Expert and Master spells, sold and learned at those ranks, instead of Apprentice.

title: A crash no longer eats your beast form

sections.heading: Beast form
items: If your game crashes or you log out while in beast form, the time you had left is kept. Your next change the same in-game day lasts for that time and does not use up the day's change. Your total time in beast form per day stays the same as before.

sections.heading: Beast form
items: A werewolf or Vampire Lord who is downed or killed in beast form no longer wakes up still looking like a beast on their own screen while everyone else sees them as mortal. Their own form is sent again once they are back on their feet.

sections.heading: Magic colleges
items: The College of Whispers and the College of Winterhold have a new first rank, Initiate, below their others; the Synod already had one. New members join as Initiates. Nobody's current rank changes.

Buying spell tomes is now earned: the court mage sells them to mages above Initiate, so ask your college's leaders about promotion. Smiths and robe-makers of a college buy none. Tomes found by reading are unchanged.
A college's leaders and officers see a fifth tome on the court mage's weekly shelf.

title: Schematics move to the forge, tomes to the ledger

sections.heading: Schematics
items: The Scholars' Ledger in the Synod Conclave no longer sells smithing schematics. A Scholar can still copy out a schematic they have learned there.
A blacksmith's ledger sells the basic schematics, starting with Steel. The first one arrives with the next plugin update. Ancient Imperial schematics are found in Cyrodiil's forts.
Your Blacksmithing page in the F3 journal says where each schematic comes from now.

sections.heading: Spell tomes
items: Spell tomes are now bought from a button on the Scholars' Ledger in the Synod Conclave: use the ledger and choose Buy spell tomes. The shelf, prices and the one tome a week are unchanged.
The /tomes command still opens the shop for a while, and reminds you to use the ledger.

sections.heading: Where the gold goes
items: When a ledger sells a schematic or a tome, the hold takes its tax, a tenth of the price leaves the world to keep gold from piling up, and the rest goes to the treasury of the faction whose hall the ledger stands in: tomes bought at the Synod's ledger pay the Synod.
A ledger in any other building pays the building's owner into their bank account, even when they are offline. A building nobody owns pays the hold.

title: Schematics in ruins and boss chests

sections.heading: Where schematics turn up
items: To read a schematic your Blacksmith craft tier must reach its tier, as well as the Scholar tier it needs. Read too early, the book stays with you. A schematic is used up once you learn from it, like a spell tome.

Schematics books now turn up as loot, in the places their craft comes from. The big chests of Cyrodiil's forts hold Ancient Imperial and Steel; Nordic barrows hold Ancient Nord and Nordic; Dwemer ruins hold Dwarven; Falmer hives hold Falmer (Honed Falmer from Adept up); Ayleid ruins hold Ayleid (Adept and harder); goblin camps hold Goblin.
Boss chests: Steel and Silver on Novice, Elven and Mithril on Adept, and Glass, Steel Plate and Gilded Elven on Expert and Master. Master boss chests very rarely hold Ebony or Daedric.
Some crafts never drop: Dragon, Madness and Aetherium are taught in roleplay, Orcish only by an Orc Blacksmith, and Stalhrim, Amber and Glacial Crystal are learned from a smith who knows them.
