Your Blacksmithing page in the F3 journal now says where each schematic is found.

sections.heading: The College of Whispers
items: The Class Lectern in Frostcrag Spire now names the College of Whispers, not the Synod.

sections.heading: Blacksmith
items: Blacksmiths now have 7 craft tiers, from Basic (wood, hide, leather, iron) to Mythic (Dragon, Daedric, Madness). Your tier grows with your Blacksmith skill.
Each material family above the basics is a technique you learn: read its Schematics book, or learn it as an apprentice by forging 10 pieces next to a Blacksmith of 75 or more who knows it.
Orcish smithing is taught only by an Orc Blacksmith. Dragon and Madness techniques come from staff only.
Schematics books: Scholars read them; the Synod sells the common ones, and rare ones turn up in ruins, forts, goblin camps and boss chests.
Improving gear at the workbench or grindstone is capped: up to two tiers above the item's own, never past tier 5, and only as far as your own craft tier.
Your Blacksmithing page in the F3 journal shows your tier, what you know and where to learn the rest (with client 0.3.90).
Smiths from before this update keep their experience: the first time you log in, you learn every technique your craft tier already allows (Orcish only for Orcs). You are told which ones.
A faction's own Blacksmith can forge that faction's armour and weapons at any craft tier, without learning the technique first.
Schematics books are used up like spell tomes: the book disappears a moment after you learn from it. A book you already know stays yours.

sections.heading: Crafting
items: About 580 weapons and armour pieces that could not be made before now have forge recipes.
New metal sets: Bronze, Copper, Brass, Adamantium and Mithril.
Leftover materials have a use: Tin and Copper make Bronze, Dwemer scrap smelts to Dwarven metal, exotic hides tan to leather, salt rock gives salt.
Quicksilver veins in Frostiron Mine and Adamantium veins in Gutted Mine; Jade turns up in loot; every troll drops its skull.
Backpacks, satchels and pouches can be made at the loom (Lore-friendly accessories by Everglaid).
Butter churns give Butter and milk jugs give milk. (Corrected 14 Oct: no churn or milk jug stands yet in a Bruma farmhouse you can reach.)

sections.heading: Sancre Tor
items: Sancre Tor's ruins have a navmesh now, so the undead chase you instead of standing still.

sections.heading: Performance
items: 163 dungeon lights in the 14 heaviest dungeons no longer cast shadows, for better frame rates.
Your game no longer runs enemies that are dead or far away.
Several server freezes of up to 5 seconds are gone.
Enemies no longer switch back and forth between players every few seconds when you walk away from them, which cut a steady stream of server work and could make them twitch.

sections.heading: Factions
items: The Imperial Civil Commission: Civil Commissioner, Praetor, Magistrate, Agent-Inspector and Clerk.
The Penitus Oculatus: Commander, Inspector, Agent and Recruit. The Emperor's own eyes; they answer to him alone.

sections.heading: Character creation
items: The Maormer are their own race now, with pale, blue-grey skin and a little shorter than the Altmer (with client 0.3.90).

sections.heading: Prayer
items: When a god answers your prayer, the message now says what the blessing does.

sections.heading: Scholar
items: Reading never hands you a spell tome you already know or are carrying.
Tomes of your own magic schools turn up three times as often: Destruction, Conjuration and Illusion for Arcane, Restoration and Alteration for Priest.
Adept Scholars can now find Apprentice tomes as well as Novice ones; Masters still find up to Adept.
Tomes are a chance on each reading, better at a higher Scholar tier, with at most 2 a day. The message now says so.
Bad luck protection: after 100 readings without a tome, the next reading brings one (still at most 2 a day).

sections.heading: Scholar
items: When your Scholar cannot rise right now, a book tells you so before the reading starts, and says when you can read again: after a short rest, after midnight (UTC), or once your Wheel has room.
Smithing schematics can still be read at any time.

sections.heading: Bruma
items: The Thalmor Embassy's halls and barracks are part of the Bruma region now: entering no longer sends you back outside.

sections.heading: Goblins
items: Goblin shamans no longer drop their staves.
A fallen goblin keeps most of its weapons and gear: each piece comes with the body only about one time in four. Goblin wax is unchanged.

title: The dead walk at Sancre Tor

sections.heading: Sancre Tor and Minotaur's Rest
items: The minotaurs are gone: they stood and stared instead of fighting.

The old Imperial fort town's dead have risen in their place: skeletons and zombies, in greater numbers than the minotaurs were, with stronger zombies where the Minotaur Lords stood. They hit hard and take punishment.

sections.heading: Lockpicking
items: The higher the lock, the more pins you have to set: Novice 2, Apprentice 3, Adept 4, Expert 6, Master 8.

sections.heading: Werewolves
items: Howl of Terror and the detect-life howl now work for everyone around you, not only for the creatures your own game runs.

title: Open Lock spells work on dungeon chests

sections.heading: Magic
items: Open Apprentice Lock, Open Expert Lock and Open Master Lock now open a locked chest in your dungeon claim: face the chest within about 12 metres and cast. Each opens locks of its own level and below.
They work on dungeon chests only, not on jail cells or house doors.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Rabbits no longer count towards mudcrab bounties, and Bruma posts fewer mudcrab bounties than before (fox spots had been read as mudcrab country).

sections.heading: Journal (F3)
items: Your Profile tab has a Status section: level and points to spend, hunger, rest buffs, Death's Chill, jail time, rerolls, skill boost, vampire and Hunt rank, and the dungeons resting for you. No more /status, /chill or /hunger.
Help buttons under it: spend level points, call a GM, report a problem, or get unstuck, without typing a command.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Your field of view from the launcher is checked again after every load and set back if the game changed it.
Creatures keep their weapons in hand.
Summons follow you properly indoors instead of standing still.
Other players hear your shouts: the Thu'um plays with the shout, one, two or three words.

sections.heading: Conjuration
items: Summons and raised dead now grow with your Conjuration rank. A Novice's summon takes 40% less damage and hits 20% harder; a Master's takes 70% less and hits twice as hard.
A single bite or spell no longer wipes out a summon it would not have killed after that reduction.
Summons last longer too: from 50% longer at Novice to three times as long at Master.

sections.heading: Journal
items: The journal's Stats tab (F3) now opens on Current Effects: the time left on Death's Chill, then your hunger, Well Rested and Well Fed, and any jail sentence.
Undead characters resist Death's Chill as a disease, so it never showed among their active effects even though it still weakens them. It is listed here now.

sections.heading: Dungeons
items: The magic barrier in Echo Cave is back. Pulling its chain still drops it, and it now returns for the next party when the claim on the cave ends, instead of staying down for good.

sections.heading: The world
items: Going into Moranda no longer sends you back as if you had left the Bruma region.

sections.heading: Woodcutting
items: A chopping round gives twice the firewood (6 for a Novice up to 16 for a Master), and a block rests for 5 minutes instead of 10.

sections.heading: Loot
items: Camp chests (Sancre Tor Ruins, Minotaur's Rest, the giant camps) now hold common ingredients only. Rare finds like Jarrin Root and Nirnroot stay out in the world and in dungeons.

sections.heading: Creatures
items: The minotaurs of Sancre Tor and Minotaur's Rest attack on sight, and are a little tougher than an ordinary minotaur: they hit hard and take less than half of every blow.

title: Moranda and the Sancre Tor Ruins

sections.heading: Moranda
items: A new Ayleid ruin near Bruma: Moranda. Claim it at its door like any other dungeon, for a party of up to six.
Skeletons and Ayleid undead guard its halls, and an Ayleid lich waits at the end beside its treasure. On Novice a lesser undead takes the lich's place.

sections.heading: Sancre Tor Ruins
items: The ruins of Sancre Tor, near Bruma, are now a world dungeon: open to everyone, no claim needed, and overrun by minotaurs, Minotaur Lords among them.
Minotaurs come back about half an hour after they fall. The ruin's eight chests, three of them boss chests, refill for each player every hour.
Minotaurs also hold Minotaur's Rest, with a chest of their own.

sections.heading: Cooking
items: Ovens are Cook stations, like cooking pots: only a Cook can bake. Castle Bruma's kitchen has a new oven and cooking pot.

sections.heading: Dungeons
items: Big dungeons no longer wake all at once. The enemies at the entrance and the boss's room are there when you arrive as before; the rest appear in their own rooms, a group at a time, before you get near them. A solo run (or a small party) no longer has to run the whole dungeon's enemies at once, which should make places like Serpent's Trail much smoother. Small dungeons are unchanged.

sections.heading: Enchanting
items: Enchantments you learned by disenchanting now show at the arcane enchanter again after you log back in. The game remembers an enchantment by its base record, and the server only gave back its effects.
If yours are still missing, type /syncenchant once while you are in the world.

sections.heading: Alchemy
items: Alchemists can now brew drinks: crouch and use an alchemy lab to open the Brewing list. Standing, the lab works as before.

Novices brew ale, beer, mead, cheap wine and mazte; Apprentices add juniper mead, wine, Alto wine, spiced wine, shein and flin; Adepts add Black-Briar and Honningbrew mead, Dragon's Breath, Cyrodilic and Colovian brandy, Firebrand, Surilie Brothers and Shadowbanish wine, sujamma and skooma; Experts add double-distilled skooma.

Drinks are made from what grows and is gathered: wheat, honeycomb, grapes, jazbay, juniper, snowberries, comberries, saltrice, fire salts and moon sugar. The list marks any drink you lack the ingredients for.
Skooma is forbidden in the Empire, and every batch brewed is written in the staff log.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Your face no longer changes after you open RaceMenu: the game keeps your own face when it swaps in a default head.
Ingredient stacks that could not be dropped or stored (extra copies of salt and others) are cleared: what you see now matches what you really hold.
Dungeon chests no longer stack their outline every time you pass a door, which made them blinding and laggy.
Torches held by other players no longer pile up light the longer you stand near them.

sections.heading: New
items: While someone talks on voice chat, their name turns green with a <)) mark.
Trading: a slider (with Half, -10 and +10) to choose how many of an item to trade.

sections.heading: Skills
items: Waxing, Held and Waning are now called Raise, Hold and Lower, with a one-line explanation each in the Wheel.

A skill set to Lower can now give its points all the way down to level 1 (it stopped at 25 before), so you can move points out of a skill you no longer use. Raised skills still stop at 25, and held skills never give points away.

sections.heading: Crafting
items: The Imperial General's set, the Emperor's set, the Imperial Legate Armor and the Imperial Officer's Cloak are now Imperial Legion gear: only the Legion's smiths, tailors and leader make them, and they no longer come from loot or get swapped.

title: Placed chopping blocks play the mini-game

sections.heading: Woodcutting
items: Chopping blocks staff have placed (Fort Caractacus, Bruma) now run the woodcutting mini-game and rest like every other block, instead of handing out firewood endlessly.

sections.heading: The world
items: Walking past the edge of the alpha region now brings you back to where you last stood inside it, instead of letting you wander off the map.

title: Real trees around Bruma, Fort Coldcorn and the border

sections.heading: The world
items: Around 2,300 blurry far-away trees near Bruma and the border are now real trees you can walk up to.
Fort Coldcorn's broken wall is fixed, and the map markers for Mountain Watch, Frostiron Mine, Echo Cave and Fort Coldcorn sit in the right places.
Frostiron Mine is a working mine, not a dungeon: it can no longer be claimed as one.
The Bruma border has moved out to take in more of the surrounding land.

sections.heading: Enchanting
items: Disenchanting something no longer makes you forget the enchantments you had already learned. They come back on their own a moment later, so there's no need for /syncenchant after each one.
Disenchanting now trains the Enchanter skill, as it does in Skyrim.

sections.heading: Crafting
items: A faction's own smiths and its leader can now make the faction's gear at any forge, wherever its designs come from: the Dawnguard can make Dawnguard armour and weapons in Bruma. Other gear still follows the province rules.
The Dawnguard's smiths can also make the silver weapons of the Silver Hand (silver longswords, katanas, war axes and the rest). The Mantle of the Silver Hand stays the Silver Hand's.
Crossbows are the Dawnguard's: only its smiths and leader make them (plain, enhanced and dwarven), and crossbows no longer come from loot or get swapped. Bolts stay open to every smith.

sections.heading: Factions
items: Every faction's armour and weapons now match, ready for wars: light faction armour is as good as Glass, heavy as Steel Plate, shields as Orcish (heavy) or Glass (light), and faction weapons hit like the Glass weapon of their type. The Imperial Legion goes up; the Dawnguard, the Blades and most Orc clan gear come down to the same level.
Orc clan gear belongs to the strongholds' clans.

sections.heading: Enchanting
items: When the server refuses an enchantment, it now tells you why. Fortify Alchemy and Fortify Enchanting can't be put on items on this server. You may also lack the Enchanter skill, the item may not take an enchantment, or the server may not know the effect. The item always keeps its previous state, and no soul is used.
Dragonborn's Chaos Damage enchantment can now be put on weapons. Like every crafted enchantment, it is held to the base game's limits.

sections.heading: Spells
items: Summon Will-o-the-Wisp is still switched off because the wisp crashes the game. Anyone who still had it loses the spell the first time they try it, it can't be prepared again, and its tome is no longer sold.

sections.heading: Restraints
items: Bound hands stay bound: if a captive's pose breaks (a hit, a door, water, a seat), it comes back within a few seconds, for shackles and rope alike.

sections.heading: Dungeons
items: Serpent's Trail: walking into its closed exit towards Skyrim no longer freezes you; you are taken back to Bruma.

sections.heading: Priest
items: At Priest 25 you now choose your first Restoration spell from Healing, Lesser Ward and Insect Swarm. If you passed 25 and were told there was nothing to choose, you will be offered the choice now.

sections.heading: Smelting and woodcutting
items: Smelting steel-tier and better metals needs charcoal: 1 per ingot for steel, silver, corundum and dwarven, 2 for gold, orichalcum, moonstone, quicksilver and malachite, 3 for ebony and stalhrim. Iron, copper and tin need none. Short of charcoal, the smelter burns 3 firewood for each one missing. Woodcutters make charcoal at the chopping block, more at each tier.
Chopping blocks and the everyday seams (iron, copper, tin, corundum and salt) now rest for each player separately, so nobody has to race for them. Precious and rare ores and geodes are still shared.

sections.heading: Vampires
items: After feeding, you can draw your weapon again straight away instead of having to re-equip it.
Feeding on bodies can be turned off: /feed off makes E search a body instead, /feed on brings feeding back.

sections.heading: Dungeons
items: Skeletons and zombies can now be searched: they often carry bone meal, and sometimes a few coins or an ingredient.

sections.heading: Storage
items: Gear kept in a chest outside the dungeons is no longer changed: crafted Steel Plate (and anything above steel) stays as it is. Only dungeon loot is capped at steel.

sections.heading: Dungeons
items: Lootable and locked chests in a dungeon you have claimed are outlined, so you can spot them.

sections.heading: Factions
items: A character now serves one faction of each kind: one allegiance (a hold's court, the County of Bruma's court, the Imperial Legion, the Stormcloaks, the Thalmor, the Blades or a Great House), one guild, and one secret society or Daedric cult. Living in a hold as a Citizen or a Guard does not count: a Legion soldier may be a citizen of Bruma, but not sit in its court.

Some loyalties can never mix: the Legion and the Stormcloaks, the Thalmor and the Blades, the Dawnguard and vampires, the Vigil of Stendarr and the Daedric cults, the Synod and the College of Whispers. If you are refused, you are told which faction to leave first. Nobody loses a membership they already hold.

Officers, leaders and sergeants of the Imperial Legion, the Stormcloaks, the Thalmor, the Blades and the Great Houses, and every hold Guard, Guard Sergeant and Guard Captain, may now restrain and arrest.

sections.heading: Crafting
items: Orcish armour and weapons are an Orc's work: only Orc characters (vampire Orcs included) can make them at a forge. Anyone can still temper Orcish gear they own, and a refused craft gives your materials back when you close the menu.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Werewolf and Vampire Lord claws hit as hard as they should again. Since the last update they were dealing the damage of a mortal's fists.
A werewolf no longer goes feral or answers the full moon in the first five minutes after logging in.

A werewolf gets 45 seconds' warning, with the ground shaking, before the beast takes them, and a sated werewolf is never taken at all: only hunger and the full moon force the change. /syncenchant resends the enchantments you have learned to your arcane enchanter if they ever go missing.
/syncenchant now says how many learned enchantments it sent, or that none are recorded for your character yet. Using it no longer risks a later disenchant taking a second copy of an item.
The Statue of Meridia near Namira's shrine in Bruma's hills can't be touched. Stand beside it and say /pray to pray to Meridia, or to take her as your god with /deity Meridia afterwards.
Goblins in a claimed dungeon can now be searched: press E on a fallen goblin to take what it carried, as you would a bandit. Until now only goblin bosses and guards could be searched.

Teaching spells: only a Master (Arcane Arts, or Priest for its schools) can teach a spell, and only spells of Adept rank and above. The student must be able to learn it already, as if reading its tome: the right tier for its rank and enough study of its school.

The Synod's tome shop shows only tomes you can learn right now, four at a time. The shelf changes every Monday (UTC), and everyone at the shop sees the same shelf that week. It is still one tome a week, at the same prices.
Smelting burns firewood: each ingot made at a smelter costs 2 Firewood, which woodcutting gives. Without enough, the smelt is refused and your ore comes back when you close the menu.

sections.heading: Magic
items: Your schools of magic show how far you are towards the next level, beside the rank in Study Magic and the journal (for example "Apprentice · 40% to 37"), and Study Magic's meter fills with it.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Spells cost their magicka again for High Elves and for anyone under a blessing or the Ayleid well's starlight. Their extra regeneration no longer handed back the magicka of a spell just cast.

Hunting contracts are now your own: taking a notice no longer takes it from anyone else, and you can hold up to three at once (each notice once). Every hunter keeps their own count and is paid their own reward from the hold's treasury, and one kill counts for every contract it fits. A hold no longer gives out bounties that would empty its treasury. A kill that does not count, because the creature is not your quarry or fell outside the hold's wilds, now says so. Boards post up to twice as many notices, and they turn over twice as fast.
The time left in Study Magic and Priest Studies now counts down while you study. Before, it jumped back up every few seconds.
Faction armour and clothing: 88 new recipes for faction sets are in the game. Only the faction's own Armorer or Clothier can make them, and a Great House's sets once that House is claimed.
A vampire who has fed recently looks mortal again: their own eyes and their own colour. The glowing eyes and the pallor only show from the third stage of thirst, and feeding takes them away again.
A vampire newly turned by the fever shows them until their first meal. The sun still burns every vampire, fed or not.

Switching to another character more than 15 minutes after you connected now sets that character up properly. Before, it skipped the login steps: enchantments you had learned did not show at the arcane enchanter, and your party, faction and other login messages never arrived. Those enchantments come back the next time that character logs in, including the ones being given back from before 4 October.

sections.heading: Holds and strongholds
items: A ruler, Guard Captain or Chieftain can now appoint as many Guards or Stronghold Guards as their hold needs. Before, each hold stopped at 20.

sections.heading: Factions
items: The Great Houses of Morrowind are factions now, ready to be claimed: Hlaalu, Redoran and Telvanni with their ranks from Morrowind, and Indoril, Dres and Sadras with the Great Houses' shared ranks. Each has an Armorer and a Clothier.

title: The Synod sells only tomes you can learn

sections.heading: Magic
items: The Synod's tome shop no longer sells a spell tome that your study of its school is not yet high enough to learn. The shop shows what you still need, and you keep your gold and your tome for the week.

sections.heading: No more timing mini-games
items: Mining, woodcutting and skinning no longer ask you to hit a moving marker. Each blow or cut shows a few spots on the stone, the wood or the hide; one shows the clearest sign, and choosing it lands the blow. Higher ranks see the sign more clearly and fewer false ones.

The same goes for struggling against bound hands (pull where the rope gives), picking a lock (find where the pins give), prayer (choose the verse that belongs to your god), the vampire and werewolf rites (read the marks of the rite) and reading a book (a wrong reading burns a candle stub, not seconds).
Nothing depends on how fast your computer or your connection is any more.

sections.heading: Smithing
items: Your Blacksmith rank now opens the forge recipes that asked for the old Smithing perks: Steel, Elven and Dwarven at Apprentice, Orcish and Advanced Armors at Adept, Glass and Ebony at Expert, Daedric and Dragon at Master. Improving enchanted gear (Arcane Blacksmith) is not part of it, and a few faction sets still wait for a plugin update.

sections.heading: Werewolves and Vampire Lords
items: Other players see a werewolf's and a Vampire Lord's beast body again.
The screen shakes as a forced werewolf change comes near, three times in the 12 seconds after the warning.

sections.heading: Summons in a fight
items: Your summons and raised dead fight another player only where PvP allows it: while you and that player are fighting, never someone in your party, downed, jailed, held or logged out.
A summon or raised body that stands still in a fight it is getting nowhere with tries again, then comes back to you.

sections.heading: Menus and keys
items: Trading asks how many for any stack of two or more, so you can trade one item from a stack.
The player menu (X) closes when the player you opened it on walks away or leaves.
The hunger and voice panel fades with the health bars when you set the bars to fade.
The Place tool's preview no longer flickers while you aim.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Fewer crashes and black screens while loading into a busy area: the game no longer removes another character's copy while it is still being drawn or while a loading screen is up.
A dropped enchanted weapon keeps the charge it really has.
A disenchant made just before you close the arcane enchanter is no longer lost.
Talking now carries as talking and shouting as shouting: each voice is at full volume over a fifth of its range.
Howl of Terror is taken away on every way out of werewolf form.
Two crashes when another player's character was thrown into a ragdoll as it appeared are fixed.

sections.heading: Character slots
items: Play 150 hours on DragonBreak Online and you earn an extra character slot, yours to keep. The hours of all your characters count together.
Your hours count from the opening of the alpha on 1 October, so the time you have already played counts too.
The slot comes on top of any slots your Patreon tier or roles give you. You are told when you earn it, and it appears on the character screen the next time you log in.
Type /playtime to see your hours so far.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Reading a spell tome early no longer closes the study shelves. Priest Studies and Study Magic keep teaching until the skill reaches 25, even if you already learned a spell from a tome; from 25 your skill grows by casting, in prayer and in class as before.
Werewolf and Vampire Lord forms train no skills: claws are not fists, and nothing a beast does counts toward a skill or a school of magic.
Reading tells you when you have found all the books, scrolls or spell tomes you can for the day (6 copies, 6 scrolls and 2 tomes); finds come back at midnight UTC, and reading still trains Scholar.
Killing animals no longer trains Skinner. Skinning and tanning still do.
For 20 seconds after you log in, creatures cannot hurt you while the world loads in around you. Attacking or casting ends it early.
When the beast takes a werewolf without asking (hunger or the full moon), you are warned 12 seconds before the change.
Anyone in werewolf or Vampire Lord form goes only by Werewolf or Vampire Lord, never their own name.
The Bloodscale Bone Helmet no longer drops as loot: for now it only fits Argonians and Khajiit.
Enchantments a few characters learned at the arcane enchanter before the 4 October update come back at their next login.
Weapons you enchant with Soul Trap yourself now trap souls: a kill while the effect lasts fills an empty soul gem, as weapons found with Soul Trap already did.
Raise Zombie tells you when a body cannot rise: one too powerful for the spell, another adventurer's, or one already bound.

Inside a house, each chest and inner door now has its own key, cut at that chest or door. A key cut at a door in from the street opens the doors in from the street; inner doors and chests use their own keys. The owner still opens them all.

Gear you make, buy or trade is no longer swapped for steel when you log in, and chests inside a claimed home are left alone. The steel cap still holds for loot: dungeon chests, bodies and camps, and world chests as they are opened.

sections.heading: In the world
items: You kneel while you pray at a shrine, turn the pages while you read a book, and crouch at the body while you skin it.

sections.heading: Loot
items: College robes (Winterhold and Whispers), the Archmage's robes and the Synod's robes and hood no longer turn up in dungeons, on bodies or in camp chests. They are given by the colleges and the Synod in roleplay. Robes you already have are yours to keep.
Ordinary mage robes still drop as before.

sections.heading: Economy
items: Gold was coming into the world about seven times faster than it was being spent, so the coin you get from fighting is cut to about a quarter. Prices stay the same, so a house, a tax bill or a new look at /appearance is worth working towards again.
Champion beasts pay 5 to 20 gold a kill, shared among the fighters (was 25 to 120).

Dungeons and expeditions: chests, urns and bodies hold coin less often and less of it, about 60% less a clear. A cleared Bruma dungeon pays roughly 20 gold on Novice and 75 on Master, on top of everything else it holds.
Coin purses hold 3 to 12 gold (was 8 to 30), and goblin and giant camp chests 4 to 10 (was 8 to 22).
Gold you already have is not touched.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Enchantments you learn by disenchanting are kept when you log out: the next time you log in your character still knows them at the arcane enchanter.
A robbery demand is dropped when the robber walks away before you answer: your panel closes and you keep everything.

Keys have real names. A property with no name of its own cuts keys called after its building, such as Key to Bruma Castle, and every key cut gets its own number, so keys never stack and you can tell which is which. Keys you already have keep working.

A locked chest in a dungeon or expedition always holds something once you pick it: about a third of them used to open on nothing, and those now hold coin. Coin purses inside fill again for each new claim, so a party that claims straight after another no longer finds every purse emptied.
Some enemies in Underpall, Red Ruby Cave, Fort Cutpurse, Anga, Niryastare, Plundered Mine and Silorn failed to appear on their first try and turned up a little later. They now appear with the rest.

After changing your school of magic, Study Magic at the shelves teaches your new school until you learn a spell of it. Before, a spell of your old school kept the shelves closed ("You have learned ...; the shelves have nothing more to teach you").
If the GM who took your call logs off, your call goes back to waiting for the next GM after three minutes, and you are told.

sections.heading: Characters
items: New command: /appearance reopens the appearance editor for your own character. A new look costs 500 gold, and you can change it once a day. Closing the editor without changing anything costs nothing.
Your race, sex and name stay as they are. For a new name, ask a GM.
It can't be used in a fight, inside a dungeon, or while down, jailed or bound. This was the most-voted idea in #suggestions: thank you for voting!

sections.heading: Property
items: Owning a house now means owning all of it: its doors in from the street and its rooms inside, upstairs and below. Every door and chest inside is yours without being granted one by one (one that another player already owns there stays theirs), and handing the house over or giving it up takes everything inside with it.

Chests inside open only for you (and the hold's property officials) unless you share one with your household or give it to someone from the property menu's Rooms and chests. Doors inside stay open unless you lock them or give them to someone.

Aim at a door or chest inside and press the housing key: Lock locks just that one. Naming, keys, handing over and giving up act on the whole house from anywhere inside it. Locking a door in from the street locks every way in, not the doors inside.
Each player holds one property, and only a building counts: a chest or a room door granted on its own is not a property. Nobody loses anything they hold today.

A faction's hall owned by the faction's leader is shared with its members, as Frostcrag Spire is with the College of Whispers and the Fighters Guild hall with the Fighters Guild: members sleep in its beds and open, lock and use its chests and doors as the owner does. Members cannot hand it over, give it up, rename it or cut its keys.
Every bed in any of a house's rooms is its owner's own bed.

sections.heading: Property
items: A house with several doors was taxed once for each of them in the weekly reckoning. A house now pays its property tax once, and the treasury's report lists it once.

title: Faster Mining, Smithing, Skinning and Priest

sections.heading: Skills
items: Mining a vein now counts twice as much toward your Miner skill.

Iron-tier smithing and smelting (iron, copper and leather gear, horseshoes and fittings, and smelting iron, copper, corundum and tin ore) now counts two and a half times as much toward Blacksmith. Smelting silver, gold, ebony and the other higher ores counts as before.
Skinning, tanning and hunting animals now count half as much again toward Skinner.
Casting Restoration and Alteration spells and praying now count a quarter more toward Priest.
Your hourly and daily skill limits are unchanged: the same work simply moves you further.
Remaking an item you broke down in the last hour no longer counts toward your skill.

sections.heading: Frostcrag Spire
items: The expedition board in Frostcrag Spire now works. Before, it only told you to go to the Synod Conclave or the Fighters Guild in Bruma.

Set out from it like from the boards in Bruma: pick a ruin, choose the difficulty and go with your party. Party members anywhere in the Spire, its tower included, come along, and the party comes home to Frostcrag's front hall.
Its Contracts tab shows Bruma's hunting work, as the other boards do.

sections.heading: Game crashes near dragons
items: On 4 October, dragons flying near Bruma closed many players' games. Staff can no longer bring dragons into the world until the game client is fixed, so this cannot happen again in the meantime.
No dragon appears in dungeons or in the wild, so nothing else changes for you. Dragons come back once the fix is in the game client.

sections.heading: Weapons, armour and metals
items: Glass, Elven and other gear above the loot rules is now swapped for its steel or iron equivalent every time you log in, and in a container every time it is opened, not only the first time.
Enchantments still carry over to the replacement, and staff-granted artifacts are still left alone.
Dwarven metal ingots, which you smelt from Dwarven scrap, are now kept like the ores you mine: they are no longer swapped for steel. They still never come from loot.

title: Call a GM from the game

sections.heading: Contact a GM
items: Need staff? Type /gm and what you need, or press U and choose Contact a GM under Help & trouble. Every staff member in the game is told at once, with where you are standing.
When a GM takes your call you are told who is on the way. /gm on its own shows your call, /gm with more words adds to it, and /gm cancel withdraws it.
If no staff are online, your call waits for the first one who logs in. For anything that needs a record, such as a player report, /ticket still opens a private ticket on Discord.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: The U menu is up to date: your journal and its keys, magic, mining and smelting, rites and cures, homes and courts are all in it, and Help & trouble has a button for each kind of ticket. Before, the one ticket button only listed the kinds.

Enemies and other NPCs in Fort Cutpurse, Northfringe Sanctum, Underpall and other dungeons no longer slam a door open and shut over and over when they come through it. Once an enemy opens a door it stays open, and you can still open and close it yourself.

sections.heading: Interface
items: The gold count is gone from the HUD panel. Your inventory shows your gold as before.

sections.heading: One journal, every tab
items: F3 opens your journal, which now has a tab for each part of your character's life: Profile, Faction, Court, Stats, Skills, Magic, Deity, Supernatural and Settings. It opens on the tab you used last.
Faction and Court show when you belong to one, Magic once you have taken up Arcane Arts or Priest, and Supernatural for vampires, werewolves and anyone carrying their disease.

sections.heading: Skills
items: K now opens the Skills tab of your journal: the Wheel, your skills and their tiers, with the same choices as the old skills window.

sections.heading: Magic
items: The Magic tab shows your five schools of magic with their level and rank and which tomes your rank lets you read, your prepared spells, every spell you know, and a few tomes to look for next.
You can pick a school's first spell here too, anywhere outside a fight. Prepared spells are still changed at a Scholars' Ledger.

sections.heading: Deity
items: The Deity tab lists every god and faith: what they rule, their boon, their shrines in Bruma, and where their worship breaks the law. You can turn to a new god from here, with the same 7-day wait as before, and /deity opens it.

Talos' entry gives the law as it stands in 4E 211: under the White-Gold Concordat his worship is outlawed throughout the Empire, and Bruma is Imperial land. North of the Jerall Mountains each Jarl now decides for their own hold.

sections.heading: Court and Faction
items: If you hold an office or a place in a hold's household, or someone has offered you a post, the Court tab shows your court: its offices and who holds them, its free seats and its household. A ruler appoints, dismisses and moves people from here, and you accept or decline an offered post here.
A hold's household now shows on the Court tab rather than the Faction tab.
A faction's leader can rename the faction's rank titles on the Faction tab.

Staff can now rename an office or a rank in any hold, stronghold or faction, for example a Steward to a Reeve. The new name shows at once for everyone who holds it, in the journal and in appointments, and staff can set it back to the original.

sections.heading: Settings
items: General: change your menu keys, such as chat, journal, skills, emotes and push to talk. New keys take effect the next time you start the game. There is also a new Hide chat key, unset until you choose one.
Controls: the game's own keys are listed here, and you still change them in the launcher.

Voice, while voice chat is on: your microphone and speakers, your volume and everyone else's, push to talk or voice activity, and a volume for each player near you. In the X menu, Voice settings for a player opens this page at their name.

Interface: show your health, magicka and stamina always, only when they are not full, or never, in the Quiet or the Classic style; show the chat always, only while it is in use, or only once you press T; and pick its lettering.
Help: report a problem from here. It sends the same report as /bug.

sections.heading: Interface
items: Everyone now starts with the quieter look. Your health, magicka and stamina bars are thinner and muted, fade out a few seconds after all three are full, and come back as soon as one drops. The chat fades when you are not using it and uses book lettering.
Prefer the old look? Switch back in F3, Settings, Interface. A choice you save there stays.
The chat window is restyled to match the journal.
The X menu's entries are grouped under headings: Party, Faction, Law, Shadows, Your nature and Voice.

sections.heading: Trading
items: The trade window sorts your things into categories, such as weapons, armour, clothing, jewellery, potions, ingredients, books, soul gems, ingots and ore, and keys.
Sort by name, value or weight, and see each side's total value and weight before you agree.

title: Magic: A First Spell for Every School

sections.heading: Your first spell, in each school
items: When one of your schools of magic reaches 25, you choose its first spell, no tome needed: Flames, Sparks or Frostbite for Destruction; Courage or Fury for Illusion; Bound Sword or Conjure Familiar for Conjuration; Oakflesh or Candlelight for Alteration.
Restoration is the priest's school: when your Priest skill reaches 25, you can take Healing as your first Restoration spell.
Your school starts at your Arcane Arts level, so if you choose it at 25 its first spell follows straight away. A secondary school starts at 33, so its first spell comes as soon as you choose it.
The choice opens at a Study Magic shelf, at a Scholars' Ledger, or when you log in. Spells you already know aren't offered.
If you were given a first spell when you chose your school, that was your pick for that school.
Fury turns a person or creature on whoever is near them. Inside a dungeon, enemies can't hurt each other, so it does little there.

sections.heading: Starting spells
items: Characters start out knowing no spells. Flames and Healing are learned like any other spell, and if you already know them you keep them.

sections.heading: Schools grow more slowly
items: Schools of magic now grow at about a third of their old pace, from casting and from classes alike.
Taking a school from 25 to 50 by casting alone now takes about 13 days at the daily limit.

sections.heading: Changing your school
items: You can now swap one of your schools of magic for another at a Scholars' Ledger or a Study Magic shelf, once every 7 days.
The new school starts at half the level of the one it replaces. The old school rests at its level, and if you change back later you pick it up where you left it.
Your spells stay in your spellbook and can still be prepared. You can't read the tomes of a resting school or raise it by casting.
A swap never gives you a third school.

sections.heading: Flesh spells protect you
items: Oakflesh, Stoneflesh, Ironflesh and Ebonyflesh now really protect you. While one lasts, the server counts its armour (40, 60, 80 or 100) against weapon and unarmed hits, on top of what you wear.
A new Flesh spell replaces the one before it; they don't stack.

sections.heading: Studying tomes
items: Frost Crag Spire: you can now learn spells from tomes in its study upstairs, beside the Scholars' Ledger and the Class Lecterns, as well as at the Study Magic shelf by the alchemy table.
Reading a tome too far from a study spot now tells you how far away the nearest one in that place is.

title: Vampirism and lycanthropy, rarer and clearer

sections.heading: Rarer
items: Both diseases are now rarer, and lycanthropy the rarest. A werewolf's bite passes on Sanies Lupinus 1 time in 200. A vampire's blow passes on Sanguinare Vampiris 3 times in 100, and a vampire's feeding 1 time in 20.
Surviving Hircine's Great Hunt now marks you with Sanies Lupinus 1 time in 10.

sections.heading: The fever
items: Carrying Sanies Lupinus no longer lets you take the beast's form. The beast is yours only once the fever has peaked and you have turned.
When your fever breaks, you are now told what broke it.

sections.heading: Curing the fever
items: A Cure Disease potion still cures it, and so does food or a potion with a cure disease effect. An ingredient cures it only when curing disease is its first effect.
Prayer cures the fever only at a shrine of the Divines. Praying to a Daedric Prince or to one of the older faiths, or praying away from a shrine, no longer does.
Before such a prayer cures you, the shrine warns you. Pray again within a minute to go on.

sections.heading: Weaknesses
items: Werewolves now take extra harm from silver only in beast form: 25% more, down from 50%. In human form silver harms them as it harms anyone.
In beast form, poison spells and venom also strike werewolves 25% harder. Poison on a blade does not count.
Vampires still take more harm from silver and fire.

sections.heading: Offices
items: When a ruler or another official appoints someone to an office, it is now an offer. The person accepts or declines it: type /court offers to see yours, then /court accept or /court decline. An offer lapses after 24 hours. Staff still appoint outright.
Holding an office now gives you its rank in the hold's household, and leaving the office takes that rank away. The household ranks that offices set can't be renamed.
Holds and the County of Bruma now have a Steward rank, right under the Jarl or Count: appointing a Steward gives them that rank, and everyone already in a household keeps their rank.
Orc strongholds now have a Bane rank, right under the Chief: appointing a Bane gives them that rank, and everyone already in a stronghold keeps their rank.

sections.heading: Skills
items: A skill's third tier is now called Adept everywhere, as spells and schools of magic already call it. It used to be Journeyman.

title: Gentler dungeons on the easier difficulties

sections.heading: Dungeons
items: Enemies in dungeons and expeditions hit softer on the easier difficulties: Novice half damage, Adept about two thirds, Expert four fifths, Master unchanged. This counts for their weapons and claws, and for most of their spells.

title: A farm, a smithy and a mine

sections.heading: The world
items: Aleswell's farm is replanted: leeks, wheat, potatoes, carrots, gourds and grapes, where the old tomato beds were.
Fort Caractacus has a working smithy: a forge, an armour workbench, a sharpening wheel, and a supply chest that everyone shares.

The Bleak-Frost Mine is open a short walk west of Bruma: a new road leads to its door, and its veins can be worked for iron and corundum, with a few veins of gold for miners skilled enough to work it. Three of the iron seams at the very bottom of the mine hold meteoric iron instead, for Adept miners: smelt it into ingots at any smelter.

title: Held gold counts in the launcher

sections.heading: Launcher
items: The gold players hold, shown in the launcher, now also counts gold the server keeps for players until it is paid out: commission rewards, tenancy deposits, business takings, and charter fees and refunds.

sections.heading: Followers
items: Followers walking with you each keep their own place in a formation, so a group of them no longer crowds into one spot.

sections.heading: Bodies
items: The bodies of raiders and garrison NPCs that a GM has set loose are cleared away five minutes after they fall.

sections.heading: For staff
items: NPCs raised with /warband never harm the GM who raised them. Two GMs' warbands never fight each other unless the GMs choose opposing sides with /warband side. /warband charge sends idle followers at the nearest NPC of an enemy side.
Raiders a GM sets loose are now run by a player near them rather than by the GM.
/raid shows and clears your own raid; /raid all and /raid clear all cover every GM's.

The Place tab's search puts the best matches first. Every word you type must match, "quoted words" must appear together, -word leaves out what holds it, and mod:name keeps only mods whose file name holds it.

title: Loot keeps to the steel cap, and linen in the dungeons

sections.heading: Ingots and arrows
items: Dungeon chests, urns and camp chests no longer hold Dwarven metal, quicksilver, refined moonstone, refined malachite, adamantium or meteoric iron ingots, or Elven, Ayleid or Ancient Imperial arrows. They still hold the other materials, and iron and steel arrows, as often as before.

A goblin's or giant's body searched with E no longer hands over ingots or ores above steel, and its gear and arrows above the steel cap come as their steel or iron equivalent. Enchanted pieces keep their enchantment.

Ores you mine, and the ingots smelted from them (quicksilver, orichalcum, moonstone, malachite and ebony), are no longer swapped for steel or iron. Metals above steel still never come from loot: you mine and smelt them.

sections.heading: Linen wraps
items: Linen wraps now turn up in dungeons: 1 to 3 in about one chest in eight, more often in a boss chest, and once in a while 1 in an urn or sack. Nordic tombs hold twice as many. Linen capes, robes and hoods are made from them.

sections.heading: For staff
items: The admin panel has a left rail in place of the row of tabs, one Acting on target that every tab uses, and one search bar with category chips and match counts.

Lead GMs and above can give a player Sanguinare Vampiris or Sanies Lupinus from the panel. It starts the fever as a bite would, and it is refused for a player who already carries a disease or a curse.
Lead GMs and above can set a player's level in each school of magic.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Character creation: new characters no longer appear inside someone else, and people making a character can no longer see each other.
First spells that went missing from your spell list come back, with a message when they do. A new first spell now arrives once your game has settled after loading.
Enchanted gear swapped by the new loot rules keeps its enchantment. Pieces that were swapped plain get their enchantment back the next time you log in.
Dungeon parties face fewer extra enemies for each member.

Chests, barrels and stashes now follow the same steel cap as the gear you carry: each is checked the first time it is opened. Everyone's pack is checked once more at their next login, and enchantments are kept as before.
Iron and corundum seams give more ore and recover faster.

sections.heading: Every race has a gift
items: Each race now has a gift of its own, always with you. The server applies it, so it counts in every fight.
Gifts are off while you're in werewolf or Vampire Lord form. A vampire keeps their race's gift.
Your Defense skill, a blessing and your race's resistance together never take more than three quarters off a hit.

sections.heading: The ten gifts
items: High Elves, Aldmeri Blood: magicka comes back 25% faster.
Argonians, Hist-Blooded: poison spit and poison spells hurt half as much, and your wounds heal 50% faster while you're below 35% health.
Wood Elves, Green Pact Hunter: your bows hit 10% harder, and poison spit and poison spells hurt half as much.
Bretons, Mage-Blooded: spells, staves and scrolls used on you hurt 25% less.
Dark Elves, Ash-Born: fire hurts half as much.
Imperials, Imperial Luck: 10% more gold from chests and bodies in a dungeon you've claimed, from giant camp chests and from contract pay.
Khajiit, Claws of the Moons: your claws deal 8 more damage with every bare-handed blow.
Nords, Child of the Cold: frost hurts half as much, and stamina comes back 15% faster outdoors in Skyrim and in the Jerall Mountains around Bruma.
Orcs, Berserker Blood: below 30% health, your melee blows hit 20% harder and you take 20% less damage.
Redguards, Yokudan Endurance: stamina comes back 25% faster, and poison spit and poison spells hurt half as much.

sections.heading: The old racial powers
items: All ten racial powers, Night Eye and Voice of the Emperor included, were already switched off on this server, and your gift takes their place. They may still be in your list of powers, but they do nothing.

sections.heading: Weapons and armour
items: For now, dungeon chests, bosses, fallen enemies, expeditions and camp chests hand out weapons and armour of iron and steel only, at every difficulty, enchanted or not. That includes Cyrodiil's own steel.

Elven, Dwarven, Steel Plate, Scaled, Glass and anything better no longer drop. This holds until a proper rarity system is ready. Gear you already own above steel is swapped for steel; see the note below.
The smithing manuals in boss chests follow suit: only Steel, Silver and Chainmail for now.

sections.heading: Arrows and gold
items: Arrows are rare: they turn up about a quarter as often as before, in small stacks, and an archer's quiver seldom survives the fight.
Gold from dungeon chests, urns, bodies and camp chests is halved from now on. The gold you already have stays.

sections.heading: Weapons, armour and metals
items: Gear above the new loot rules (Elven, Glass and up, high-end ingots and ores, and arrows above steel) has been swapped for steel or iron equivalents: in your inventory when you next log in, and in containers as you open them.

Enchanted pieces keep their enchantment: a Glass Sword of Scorching becomes a Steel Sword of Scorching. Pieces that were swapped plain before this fix get their enchantment back the next time you log in. Staff-granted artifacts are untouched.

sections.heading: Learning magic
items: Magic now begins with Arcane Arts. Raise it by studying at a Study Magic shelf, such as the Synod's bookcases in Bruma. Your first sitting at the books takes up Arcane Arts, which needs a free skill point.

At Arcane Arts 25 you are ready for your first spell. Choose your school of magic, then pick that school's first spell, no tome needed. The newer note, Magic: A First Spell for Every School, lists the choices.
If you reach 25 at the books, the choice opens right there. Otherwise choose on the Arcane Arts page of your skills (K), or when you next log in.
Your school starts at your Arcane Arts level, so at 25 you can read its Apprentice tomes straight away. Until you have chosen, tomes of the four schools will not settle in your mind.
Once you have your first spell, your school grows by casting and in classes, as before.

sections.heading: Already chose a school?
items: If you chose a school before this update and have no spell of it yet, you are given its first spell: right away if you are online, or when you next log in. With a spell in your book, Study Magic has nothing more to teach you; your school grows by casting and in classes.
Nobody loses a school they have already chosen.

sections.heading: Skills
items: A skill now counts at most two thirds as much work in an hour as before, and the most it can count in a day is two thirds of what it was too. Skills that were rising as fast as they could now rise at two thirds of that pace.
Every level you have already earned is kept.

sections.heading: Magic
items: Conjure Familiar can be cast again. Some other summoning spells stay switched off for now.

sections.heading: Vampires and werewolves
items: Caught Sanies Lupinus or Sanguinare Vampiris? The skills menu (K) now has a Fever tab: how far it has grown, how much play time is left before it peaks, the trial that comes then, and how to cure it.

sections.heading: Skills
items: Archery and the other weapon skills now count the blow that kills, so a bow that drops an enemy in two shots earns both shots.

sections.heading: Factions
items: The faction window now tells you how to found a faction or a cult of your own: type /charter found <name> (or /charter cult <name>) in chat, gather your co-founders, and a GM approves it.

sections.heading: Magic
items: Staves work: a staff's spell now hits, for players and for NPCs such as goblin shamans.

sections.heading: Magic
items: Casting a scroll now uses it up and the spell takes effect, even when it is your last one. Until now a single scroll could show the cast, do nothing and stay in your pack.

sections.heading: Blessings
items: Blessings that speed up your health, magicka or stamina now really do: Akatosh, Hircine, Meridia and the Worm Cult. Until now the server pulled your bar back to its normal speed.
Hircine's blessing now says what it does: stamina comes back three times as fast.

The Hist, the Ancestors, the Yokudan Gods and the Riddle'Thar gave a racial power that the server blocks, so their blessings did nothing. Now, for as long as the blessing lasts, the Hist heal you 50% faster, the Ancestors take a quarter off the damage of fire magic, the Yokudan Gods double your stamina regeneration, and the Riddle'Thar let you see in the dark.
If a blessing left one of those old powers in your spellbook, it is taken back and you get the new blessing for the time that is left.
If you die while blessed, the blessing comes back a few seconds after you stand up.

With the new game client, a blessing's effect ends when the blessing does: when it runs out, when you take another or when you turn to another god. Until now it could keep running for hours afterwards.

title: The bank counts in the launcher's gold

sections.heading: Launcher
items: The gold players hold, shown in the launcher, now includes the gold in the bank.

title: Dressed again after a slow load

sections.heading: Characters
items: When your game takes a while to load, you no longer come into the world with your clothes and weapons taken off: your outfit is put back on.

sections.heading: Magic
items: When a corpse you raised crumbles to ash, the ash holds nothing to take.

sections.heading: Items
items: Items that only appeared to be in your pack after a dropped or harvested item are now corrected straight away.

sections.heading: Breakdown
items: Novice smiths can break down Steel and Elven gear, and about 1,300 more pieces of gear can now be broken down, among them Northern Iron.
Anything above steel gives steel ingots.
Gear with any metal in it now breaks down at the smelter, so a steel helmet gives back its steel instead of only its leather strips.

sections.heading: Enchanting
items: Enchanting with Beyond Skyrim effects such as Water Walking works again.
The Enchanter skill now says what it really covers: weapons, armour and jewellery.

sections.heading: Raised and summoned creatures
items: A raised or summoned creature that keeps getting stuck is now walked along your path, so it follows you instead of standing still.

sections.heading: Emotes
items: Lay Down works.
After you sit, kneel or lie down, the next emote you pick now plays.

sections.heading: Factions
items: In the faction window, a member's rank list now shows in full, even in a small faction.

sections.heading: Crashes
items: Fewer crashes in fights with spell-casting creatures such as draugr, above all when several players share the fight. Some crashes in shared fights remain, and we are still working on them.

sections.heading: Known issues
items: RaceMenu's own extras (its Presets tab and saved preset files, the extra sliders, sculpting, overlays and body morphs) are saved only on your own PC, so they don't carry over to your character on the server. Only the standard character creator options are saved with your character.
Enchantments you learn by disenchanting are still forgotten when you log out; a fix is on the way.

sections.heading: The doors are open
items: DragonBreak Online's alpha is open to everyone in our Discord, and it is free to play.
There will be no wipe from here on. What you earn, build and forge from tonight is yours to keep.
For now the alpha is Bruma and the lands around it, high in the Jerall Mountains. More of Tamriel opens as the alpha grows.

sections.heading: A fresh start for everyone
items: To open the alpha on even ground, every character was reset once. Skills, character levels, learned spells and schools of magic are back to the start.
Items and gold went too, and you begin with a miner's clothes and boots, a pickaxe, a woodcutter's axe and 50 gold. Every chest and container in the world was emptied.
Every house is free again for the holds' officials to grant, and whoever holds one may open a business in it anew. Guild membership starts over, and your faith is yours to choose again.
Vampirism and lycanthropy are gone: everyone begins mortal, looking as they did before the curse, and the Blood Crown lies unclaimed.
Your characters, their names, their looks and your character slots are all still yours.

sections.heading: Thank you, playtesters
items: Everyone who helped test DragonBreak Online before the alpha now has a second character slot. Your double skill progress has its own note.

sections.heading: Help and guides
items: Something wrong in game? Type /bug followed by what happened, while it's in front of you.
If the game closes or won't start, open the launcher's gear, then Troubleshooting > Report a Problem, or open a ticket on our Discord.
The guides to skills, magic, crafting, races, religion, the holds and the rules are at dragonbreakonline.com/guides.

sections.heading: Double skill progress for 24 hours
items: Everyone who helped test DragonBreak Online before the alpha gets double skill progress for 24 hours. It starts at your first login after the alpha opens on 1 October at 05:00 UTC, whichever character you play.
The 24 hours run in real time, online or not, and cover every character on your account. Type /boost to see how long you have left.
Your work still counts towards the usual hourly and daily limits; each bit of it simply moves your skill twice as far.
Log in by 8 October at 05:00 UTC to claim it.

sections.heading: Lockpicking
items: Anyone with a lockpick can now try Apprentice locks as well as Novice ones on dungeon chests, so you will meet far more locks you can work on. Adept, Expert and Master locks still need Lockpicking at that tier.
Every lock you pick works you toward Lockpicking; do it often enough and you will be offered the skill in your skills menu (K).

title: Anyone can try a Novice lock

sections.heading: Lockpicking
items: Locked dungeon chests were refusing everyone who had not already chosen Lockpicking, so nobody could pick a lock or learn the skill. Now anyone with a lockpick can try a Novice lock. Novice locks turn up on the Adept and Expert difficulties.
Picking locks works you toward Lockpicking: do it often enough and you will be offered the skill in your skills menu (K). Harder locks need Lockpicking at that tier.

sections.heading: Dungeons
items: If an Ayleid ruin's hidden stair has been raised but looks closed to you, for example after you come back from another part of the ruin, press its button again and it rises for you.

title: Safer ruin entries and contract fixes

sections.heading: Dungeons
items: Parties now enter Niryastare, Bawn and Rielle one at a time, 30 seconds apart. Loading into these ruins together was crashing players. You are told when it is your turn; if you have walked away by then, use the entrance to join your party.
If your game crashes inside a claimed dungeon, you log back in at its entrance instead of in the middle of the same fight. The claim is held for 10 minutes so you can go back in.
Joining your party in an Ayleid ruin after they opened its hidden stair now shows the stair open for you too.

sections.heading: Contracts
items: Hunting contracts now count the creature you actually killed. Rats no longer count toward a wolf contract.

sections.heading: Roleplay
items: Vampire feeding messages now name people the way you know them: someone you have not met shows as Stranger.
Pressing H now says the mask it puts on is borrowed and is handed back when you press H again.

title: Two friends at one cave mouth

sections.heading: Dungeons
items: If someone else claims a cave or dungeon while you are choosing its difficulty, you are now put back outside the entrance instead of freezing on the spot. To go in together, party up with /party invite before anyone claims it.

sections.heading: Skills
items: The playtester double-progress boost has ended early while we rebalance how fast skills grow.

sections.heading: Vampire Lords
items: Revert Form on the Shout key now turns a Vampire Lord back into their own shape. You can also type /beast to turn back at any time.

sections.heading: Vampires
items: Vampires: feeding no longer leaves your vampire spells missing after you log back in. Anyone affected gets them back automatically.

sections.heading: Lag no longer fails you
items: Praying: a prayer you held through to the end is no longer refused because your connection was slow.
Mining and woodcutting: a slow connection no longer loses a round you played. It counts even if it reaches the server minutes late.
Skinning: standing still while you skin no longer fails the cut.
Reading: a right answer now counts even if it reaches the server up to 30 seconds after the candle goes out, instead of 2.5 seconds.
Struggling against bonds: a slow connection no longer loses your pulls.

sections.heading: Lockpicking
items: The lock no longer freezes after two misses in a row, or after a try on a tumbler that is not the loose one.
Leaving a lock with Escape no longer leaves every chest and door unresponsive for a minute.

sections.heading: Rites
items: The strike window in a rite is wider and more forgiving of lag.

Until the next game update, Molag Bal's Embrace and the Great Hunt cannot be begun. A rite that can kill must not be lost to a slow connection, and the update lets your own game judge each strike. They open again with it.
Until then, losing a Blood Fever rite or Hircine's Hunt breaks the fever without killing you.

title: Three spell tomes in their proper schools

sections.heading: Magic
items: Spectral Arrow, Command Daedra and Paralyze are now ranked in their proper schools: Conjuration Apprentice, Conjuration Expert and Alteration Expert.

sections.heading: Werewolves and Vampire Lords
items: Dying in beast form: the "You're down!" panel now takes the mouse, so you can choose Give up.

sections.heading: Blessings
items: Most blessings that come as a spell are now cast on you when they are granted. Until now they only put a 'Blessing of' spell in your spellbook and did nothing.
Your blessing is cast on you again when you log back in, and again when the spell's own time (eight hours, twelve for Auri-El) runs out before your blessing does.
If you were blessed before this update, the useless spell leaves your spellbook and the blessing is cast on you instead.

sections.heading: Offerings
items: Standing up from a prayer before you begin it no longer makes the shrine rest, so you can touch a shrine, make your /offer and pray straight away.

title: A crash no longer costs you the temple

sections.heading: Falling in battle
items: A crash no longer costs you a fall: once the launcher reports the crash, your body cannot be harmed for up to ten minutes, and a fall that came after the crash wakes you where you fell, at full health, without Death's Chill. Quitting the game still counts as a fall.

sections.heading: A charter of your own
items: You can now found a faction of your own, a company or a cult. Type /charter found and a name to start its charter, or /charter cult and a name for a cult.

A charter needs three players on three different accounts: you as its Founder, who will lead it, an Officer and a Sergeant. Invite them with /charter invite and their name; they agree with /charter confirm and the charter's number.
Up to two more founding members can join it in any other role: Officer, Sergeant, Mage, Blacksmith, Tailor or Member.
Give it a purpose with /charter pitch. If you like, give it a seat: stand at a house you or another founding member owns and type /charter seat here.

Then /charter submit sends it to the GMs. Once they approve it, your faction is on the Faction page of your journal (F3), with the seven ranks from Leader to Member and a treasury of its own. There is no fee.

sections.heading: The rules
items: A faction's name must fit the world: not an existing faction, hold or region, and not one of the Elder Scrolls' own factions that are not in the game yet. Only a cult may be named for a Daedric Prince.
You have 48 hours to gather your founders and submit, and an account can be on one charter at a time. If the GMs decline a charter, its founder can file a new one after a week.
A faction's leader can ask the GMs to disband it with /charter disband and a reason. If they agree, its treasury goes to the player who founded it.
/charter on its own shows your charter and what to do next.

title: Iron Falchion out of loot for now

sections.heading: Loot
items: The Iron Falchion's model comes without its texture in Beyond Skyrim itself, so it no longer drops until we fix the model. If you already have one, it stays yours.
Camp chests now hold only weapons of their own land: a camp in Bruma gives Cyrodiil's weapons, not Skyrim's.

sections.heading: Dungeons
items: Weapons and armour from chests and enemies now match the difficulty you claim a dungeon on: iron and leather at Novice, steel and elven at Adept, steel plate and some glass at Expert, the most glass at Master.
Boss chests and masters give better pieces than the rest of the dungeon, and a harder lock guards better gear.
Ebony, Daedric, Dragon, Stalhrim and Orcish gear never drops.

sections.heading: Naming your character
items: A name may now end in a regnal number from II to X, like Titus Mede II, and the name of a character you deleted is free again at once.

sections.heading: Wildlife
items: Bruma's boars bite much less hard. A new character can now take seven bites before going down, where three were enough before.
They also go down faster: a new character with an iron sword now fells one in about six blows, where it took nearly thirty.
A creature's hit that is scaled down, such as a boar's power bite or a blow your Defense armour softens, no longer knocks you down when the smaller hit would not have.

sections.heading: Temples
items: Priests can now study Restoration at the temples' study points, the way mages use Study Magic. In Bruma, that is the Cathedral of St Martin.
The new lecterns in the temples have a Preach prompt. Sermons are coming soon, and for now that is what it tells you.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Walking into a cave mouth that you cannot enter yet (it rests for you, or another party holds it) no longer freezes you in front of it. You are set down just outside instead.

sections.heading: Update
items: Update through the launcher: there's a new plugin.

title: The Bank of Bruma Belongs to Bruma

sections.heading: Around Bruma and the land
items: The Bank of Bruma now counts as part of Bruma inside as well as out, and its doors are named: Bank of Bruma on the way in, Bruma on the way out.
Door names across the land now read properly, for example the Cathedral of St Martin in Bruma.
Camp chests are for players: their guards no longer pocket the loot.
Fort Caractacus is no longer a dungeon to claim and clear. It is the Legion's fort, and its doors open like any other.
Ebony, Daedric, Dragon, Stalhrim and Orcish gear no longer turns up in dungeon or camp loot.

sections.heading: Bruma pays its due to the Empire
items: Bruma is a county of the Empire, and from the next weekly reckoning (Sunday 00:00 UTC) the Empire takes its tithe: a tenth of the property tax collected on Cyrodiil land goes into the Imperial Legion's treasury.
The tithe is reckoned on the property tax taken that week, not on the treasury's savings, so it begins once a county's Count sets a tax. A county that taxes nothing owes no tithe.

If the Count is online at the Sunday reckoning (00:00 UTC), the reckoning message tells them what the tithe came to. Anything the treasury could not pay is owed, and taken first the next week. The Legion's own forts pay none, and Skyrim's Holds, independent since the Legion withdrew, pay nothing.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: A prayer to Mehrunes Dagon no longer breaks the fever that turns you into a vampire or a werewolf. A prayer to any other Daedric Prince never did.
The calendar now reads 4E 211 when you type /time. The Wait menu and your journal follow with the next client update.
When staff rename a character, the old name is free again, and the new name is kept for that character alone.
Rent held for an inn's owner while they are away now goes to that owner, even if the inn has changed hands since.
Only Lead GMs and above can raise or clear warbands and raids, from the Place tool as well as from chat.
Masks can't be duplicated by pressing the mask key rapidly.
Signatures can't use staff titles (such as Admin, Moderator or Game Master) or blocked words.

title: Werewolves Seen in Human Shape, For Now

sections.heading: Beast forms
items: For now, other players see a werewolf in its human shape, as they already do a Vampire Lord. A werewolf's howl could crash the game of anyone watching; the next client update fixes that, and the beasts come back once it has been tested.
Your own werewolf form looks and plays as before on your screen.

title: Steadier Beasts, and Characters That Act

sections.heading: Fixes
items: Fixed a likely cause of crashes near a werewolf howling or a Vampire Lord casting. For now, other players won't see a Vampire Lord's spell effects; the spells still hit as normal.
Your own character's name no longer changes on your screen when someone nearby puts on or takes off a mask.
Auto-run now switches off when a skinning, mining or chopping round takes the keyboard.

sections.heading: Animations
items: Characters act out everyday things: studying a notice board, and saluting when introducing themselves.
Potions and draughts no longer play a drinking animation; they still work instantly.

sections.heading: Your school
items: Mages now follow a school of magic: Destruction, Illusion, Conjuration or Alteration. Choose your first school on the Arcane Arts page of the Skills menu (K), or at a Study Magic spot. The same page shows all four school meters.
A school's meter rises as you cast its spells, and you can read a tome of that school only up to your rank in it. When Arcane Arts reaches 76 you may take up a second school.
Every spell you already know stays yours, whatever school you choose.

sections.heading: Study and classes
items: Study Magic at the Synod Conclave's bookcases and at the Study Magic spots: up to 20 minutes of study in any 4 hours, until you learn your first spell through Arcane Arts.

Class Lecterns stand in the Synod Conclave, Frostcrag Spire and the College of Winterhold's Hall of the Elements. A teacher of the Synod or the College can hold a class there, and every student in the room learns from it.

sections.heading: Alteration
items: Alteration belongs to priests and mages both. A priest takes it up through Priest; a mage who chose Alteration, through Arcane Arts.

sections.heading: Alchemist and Harvesting
items: Picking plants, mushrooms and fruit no longer trains Alchemist; it trains Harvesting only, as it always should have. Eating ingredients no longer trains Alchemist either.
Alchemist grows from working at the alchemy lab.

sections.heading: Sea Salt Deposits
items: Sea Salt Deposits now glow for Miners while they have salt to give, and go dark while the seam rests, so they are much easier to spot in the snow. Thanks to GroundedPasta for the report.

title: Dragon Bone and Scales Come From Dragons

sections.heading: Materials
items: Dragon bone and dragon scales now come only from slain dragons. Dragon gear breaks down into its other materials.

sections.heading: Cooking
items: Every dish can now be cooked in every land. Cooked Boar Meat and other dishes from Solstheim and Morrowind were refused in Bruma as foreign designs; they no longer are. What you can cook still depends on the ingredients you carry.
Gear, cloaks and metal ingots keep their homelands as before.

sections.heading: Werewolves
items: A werewolf who belongs to no pack is now a Lone Wolf. The Werewolf tab in your Skills menu (K), /hunt and /status say so, and a pack member sees their pack and rank there instead.
It is a name for now: nothing about your beast changes with it. A pack still takes you in only by invitation.

sections.heading: A vampire's first meal
items: A newly turned vampire's powers sleep until their first feed. Go more than six hours (game time) without blood and your body starts to wither: wounds and stamina recover more slowly each hour until you drink. Blood lifts it at once.
Ordinary food barely eases a vampire's hunger.

sections.heading: Feeding
items: Feeding now takes a few seconds, and you kneel over the body as you drink. The higher your blood rank, the quicker you feed. Moving away or being struck breaks the feed.
From Nightstalker you can Feed Deeply on a captive: it takes longer, heals you faster for a while and keeps the thirst away longer, and your victim blacks out.
Vampires can now ask anyone for their blood. The other player sees a prompt and can offer their neck or resist.
Feeding can leave blood around a young or hungry vampire's mouth. It stays until you wash it off in water.
Werewolves in beast form now play their feeding animation, and a feed takes a few seconds.

sections.heading: Fixes
items: When your thirst grows, Vampiric Drain in your hand now becomes the stronger drain instead of vanishing from your hand.

title: Pray or Perform the Rite at the Shrine

sections.heading: Shrines
items: Touching a shrine of Molag Bal, Hircine, Arkay or Stendarr now opens a panel: Pray, or Perform the Rite. When you can't do one of them, the panel tells you why.
Choosing a rite shows what it can cost before anything happens. Only the rite's own button (Kneel, Run the Hunt or Offer the soul gem) begins it, and Cancel takes you back. /rite still works.

title: Your Curse in the Skills Menu

sections.heading: Werewolves and vampires
items: Werewolves and vampires now have their own tab in the Skills menu (K): your rank and what the next one brings, your thirst or your beast, your first meal, and your powers.
The werewolf's howl that senses the living is now named for the Totem of the Hunt, as in Skyrim. Howl of the Pack is the howl that calls wolves.

sections.heading: Dungeons
items: Rooms that stood empty in a claimed dungeon now hold enemies of that dungeon's own kind, among them the back caves of Fingerbowl Cave and Serpent's Trail near Bruma. Where a room's own inhabitants had simply never appeared, like the goblins of Frostiron Mine, they are back where they belong.

title: The Goblins of Dusk Thorn Stand Together

sections.heading: Dusk Thorn Camp
items: The goblins of Dusk Thorn Camp no longer fight each other: they are one tribe now, and they turn on you together. Thanks to Onny for testing the camp.

sections.heading: Boars
items: The boars around Bruma no longer turn their tusks on each other: a herd sticks together now, and charges you as one. Thanks to GroundedPasta for the report.

sections.heading: Smithing and enchanting
items: How far you can temper now follows your Blacksmith rank: Fine as a Novice, Superior as an Apprentice, Exquisite as a Journeyman, Epic as an Expert, and Legendary as a Master.
How strong your enchantments can be now follows your Enchanter rank, from half the strength of the best enchantments found in the world as a Novice to twice it as a Master.
Items you have already tempered or enchanted keep what they have.

title: Dusk Thorn Camp and the Boars of Bruma

sections.heading: The wilds
items: Goblins have made camp east of Bruma: Dusk Thorn Camp. Eight goblins guard it, and their chest gives each adventurer a share once an hour. It glows while it has something for you.
Wild boars now roam the hills east of Bruma. They give boar meat and a tusk.
Eleven new Sea Salt Deposits line the rivers east of Bruma for Miners.

title: Crafting Follows the Land and Its People

sections.heading: Crafting
items: Gear is now made where it belongs. A smith in Cyrodiil can forge Cyrodilic, Imperial, Elven, Daedric, Ebony and Glass work, but not the arms of Skyrim, Morrowind or Solstheim; a refused craft keeps your materials.
A people can always make their own: an Orc forges Orcish anywhere, a Nord Nordic and Skaal work, a Dunmer chitin and bonemold, and so on for every race with a craft of its own.

title: Client 0.3.70: Contracts on the Expedition Board

sections.heading: Contracts
items: The expedition board now has a Contracts tab: read the hunting notices your area has posted, take one, see your progress and give it up, all from the board. /contract still works.

sections.heading: Getting it
items: The launcher downloads this update the next time you press Play.

title: Better Loot, Brewing Help and Saltier Deposits

sections.heading: Dungeons
items: Ordinary dungeons give their full loot again; expeditions keep their leaner chests.
A fallen warrior can now hand over the weapon or armour they were using when you search their body.
Chests that hold loot glow, and go dark once you have emptied them, not as soon as you open them.

sections.heading: Alchemy and gathering
